The row is 650 bytes against this corpus's 217-byte row median and 434-byte flag line (bloatReport over .claude/skills/*.md siblings). groups.body:
Surface: infra
**Related:** #3026, #2734, #2868, #2912, #2935, #3003, #3012, #3014, #3024, #3030, #3031, #3065, #3079

## Current State

`resolveIntegrationBranch` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js:357`) resolves the integration branch from `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`'s `integration-branch` key, then an in-process cache, then `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD`. This repo's `policy.yml` sets no `integration-branch` key, so the `origin/HEAD` read is the only source that resolves anything here. A fresh `git clone` in a cloud/Routine sandbox container leaves the local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` symbolic ref unset (`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` fails right after the clone, even though `origin` is configured and `git fetch origin main` succeeds). The resolver therefore returns `null`, and `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js:110-113` short-circuits every check with `{"skipped":[{"check":"all","reason":"no-remote"}]}`. This was observed in a scheduled `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` Routine firing. Running `git remote set-head origin -a` by hand fixes the session, but every new sandbox container hits the problem again.

The record left the choice of fix open: (a) fix provisioning, through the Setup script or the SessionStart hook, or (b) extend the resolver's fallback ladder with a network read such as `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`. Shaping-time evidence on that choice:

- The resolver is documented as offline and cheap. The `preferRemoteTrackingRef` comment above it says "this resolver must stay offline and cheap". Eight modules call it, including the SessionStart reaper, run-integrity, and the pre/post-tool-use hooks. Putting a network call inside it would put network latency on every hook path.
- `scripts/claude-cloud-setup.sh` is generated by `/claude-tweaks:init` Step 14 (`plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/step-14-cloud-routine-parity.md`) and is marked "do not hand-edit". CLAUDE.md's Cloud parity section records that the Setup script was measured not reaching scheduled Routine sandboxes, which is exactly where this failure was observed. Option (a) via the Setup script would not cover the reported case.
- `reconcile` already fetches over the network (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/shared-fetch.js`), so a one-time `origin/HEAD` repair inside reconcile costs nothing new in network terms and leaves the shared resolver offline.

## Deliverables

1. In `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js`, when `resolveIntegrationBranch` returns `null` and an `origin` remote is configured (`git remote get-url origin` succeeds), run `git remote set-head origin --auto` once, then re-resolve. Skip with `no-remote` only when no `origin` remote exists or the re-resolution is still `null`. Record which outcome occurred in reconcile's JSON result so the repair is visible.
2. Keep `resolveIntegrationBranch` itself offline. Do not add any network call to `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js`.
3. Add a test in `tests/reconcile.test.js` that builds a real fresh clone (a bare repo cloned into a temp directory, then `git remote set-head origin --delete` so `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` is absent) with no `integration-branch` policy key, and asserts that reconcile resolves a non-null integration branch instead of returning the `no-remote` skip.
4. Add a test asserting that a checkout with no `origin` remote still returns `{"check":"all","reason":"no-remote"}` unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a fresh clone with no local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` and no `integration-branch` policy key, `reconcile --json` resolves a non-null integration branch and does not return the `{"check":"all","reason":"no-remote"}` skip, with no manual `git remote set-head`.
- [ ] Reconcile's JSON result records that it repaired `origin/HEAD` when the repair ran.
- [ ] A checkout with no `origin` remote still produces the `no-remote` skip exactly as before.
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js`'s `resolveIntegrationBranch` issues no network git command (no `fetch`, `ls-remote`, or `remote set-head`).
- [ ] The fresh-clone test fails when the repair step is removed from `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js`.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed: scheduled Routines and fresh cloud sessions no longer skip every reconcile check as "no-remote" on a brand-new clone.

## Technical Approach

Repair `origin/HEAD` at the one consumer that already does network work, rather than in the shared offline resolver or the generated Setup script. `git remote set-head origin --auto` asks the remote for its HEAD and writes the local symbolic ref. After it runs, the existing offline `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD` read succeeds for the rest of the session, so the hook-path callers of `resolveIntegrationBranch` benefit too, with no change. The repair must follow the never-break-a-session invariant in `docs/hooks.md`: a failed `set-head` (no network, auth failure) degrades to today's `no-remote` skip and never throws.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` — one-time `git remote set-head origin --auto` repair and re-resolve before the `no-remote` short-circuit; record the repair in the result
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` — unchanged; `resolveIntegrationBranch` stays offline (referenced for the AC)
- `tests/reconcile.test.js` — fresh-clone fixture test and no-origin regression test

## Gotchas

- A plain `git clone` normally sets `origin/HEAD`, so the test fixture has to delete it explicitly (`git remote set-head origin --delete`) to reproduce the sandbox state. A fixture that merely clones will pass vacuously.
- Do not hand-edit `scripts/claude-cloud-setup.sh`. It is regenerated by `/claude-tweaks:init` Step 14, and the Setup script is not a reliable path into scheduled Routine sandboxes anyway.
- `git remote set-head --auto` makes a network round-trip. Keep it inside reconcile, never in `resolveIntegrationBranch`, whose callers include the pre/post-tool-use hooks.
- The repair writes a ref in the main checkout's `.git`. That is the same scope as reconcile's existing fetch, but confirm it does not run from inside a worktree against a different gitdir.
- Reconcile runs under a shared wall-clock budget (see related #3026). The `set-head` round-trip counts against it, so bound it with the same timeout reconcile's existing fetch uses.

## Original request

reconcile/dispatch Preflight: fresh clone with no origin/HEAD resolves integration branch as null ("no-remote")

## Current State
`resolveIntegrationBranch` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` (used by `reconcile` and by dispatch's Preflight) resolves the integration branch in this order: (1) `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`'s `integration-branch` key, (2) an in-process cache, (3) `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD`. This repo's `policy.yml` sets no `integration-branch` key, so step 3 is load-bearing. A fresh `git clone` of this repo in a cloud/Routine sandbox container does not set the local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` symbolic ref (confirmed: `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` fails with "not a symbolic ref" immediately after clone, even though `git remote -v` shows a working `origin` and `git fetch origin main` succeeds). Step 3 therefore returns `null`, and `reconcile --json` short-circuits every check with `{"skipped":[{"check":"all","reason":"no-remote"}]}` on the very first run in a brand-new container — observed directly in a scheduled `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` Routine firing today. Running `git remote set-head origin -a` manually fixes it for the rest of that session, but every new sandbox container hits this fresh since nothing in provisioning sets it.

## Deliverables
1. Either: the project's Setup script (`scripts/claude-cloud-setup.sh`) or the SessionStart hook runs `git remote set-head origin -a` (or equivalent) whenever `origin/HEAD` is unresolvable, before `reconcile` or dispatch's Preflight can run.
2. Or: `resolveIntegrationBranch` falls back further before giving up — e.g. `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` (reads the remote's HEAD directly over the network, no local symbolic ref required) — when the local `origin/HEAD` ref is absent.
3. Either fix is acceptable; a decision between "fix provisioning" vs. "fix the resolver's fallback ladder" is itself part of this record's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A freshly cloned checkout (no local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, no `integration-branch` key in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`) resolves a non-null integration branch via `reconcile --json`'s own checks, without a human manually running `git remote set-head`.
2. `reconcile --json` on such a fresh clone does not short-circuit with `{"skipped":[{"check":"all","reason":"no-remote"}]}` when a working `origin` remote exists and is reachable.
3. The fix is verified against an actual fresh clone (not just a checkout that already has `origin/HEAD` set from a prior fix), since that is exactly the gap this record reports.

## Release Note
Fixed: scheduled Routines and fresh cloud sessions no longer fail their first `reconcile`/dispatch Preflight pass with a spurious "no-remote" skip on a brand-new clone.

Surface: infra
**Related:** #2733, #2734, #2775, #2783, #2821, #2869, #2877, #2912, #2970, #3003, #3004, #3031, #3047, #3048, #3065, #3079

## Current State

Two shipped rules give an agent conflicting guidance on a pre-existing defect found in a file the build's diff touches, and neither says how they compose:

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:223` ("Scope and edit discipline") quotes the Working Approach sentence into every implementer dispatch: "a pre-existing bug you notice is a follow-up to report, not a fix to fold in, unless the task cannot work without it." The paragraph's own routing clause then sends a reported follow-up to the open-items ledger (blocking) or `/claude-tweaks:capture` (non-blocking), per Common Step 4, without naming the deferral gate.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/deferral-gate.md` "Bad reasons to skip a fix" says "if the file is in this build's diff, it is in scope", and its `Defer-reason:` vocabulary defines `pre-existing-outside-diff` as "a defect in a file this build's diff does not touch". `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md:105` routes the same reason the same way.

Observed in one `/flow` run (plugin 6.138.0): a review agent classified a pre-existing mismatch in two in-diff files as `pre-existing-outside-diff`, a reason reserved for files outside the diff. It then asked the parent to choose which rule governs, and the controller had to rule (it applied the gate and fixed the mismatch). Later phases of the same run deferred five similar in-diff items citing only "pre-existing", which the gate does not accept.

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` "Scope and edit discipline": add one sentence **outside** the quoted Working Approach text, stating that the quoted rule limits what an implementer changes mid-task and does not decide the reported follow-up's disposition. The follow-up is routed through `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s fix-now test before it reaches the ledger or `/claude-tweaks:capture`.
2. `plugin/skills/_shared/deferral-gate.md` "Bad reasons to skip a fix": add a bullet saying that a reported pre-existing defect in an in-diff file goes through the fix-now test like any other finding, and that "pre-existing" alone is not a defer reason. Only `pre-existing-outside-diff` (a file the diff does not touch) can defer on pre-existence.
3. Extend the existing conformance tests to pin both new sentences: `tests/working-approach-scope-discipline.test.js` for the build paragraph and `tests/deferral-gate-conformance.test.js` for the gate bullet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`'s Scope and edit discipline paragraph names `_shared/deferral-gate.md` as the deciding rule for a reported follow-up's disposition, and the three quoted Working Approach sentences stay byte-identical to `plugin/skills/init/claude-md-template.md`.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s Bad reasons list includes a bullet saying "pre-existing" alone is not a defer reason for a defect in an in-diff file.
- [ ] The `pre-existing-outside-diff` definition and the six-value `DEFER_REASONS` list are unchanged (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` still matches the gate's vocabulary).
- [ ] `tests/working-approach-scope-discipline.test.js` and `tests/deferral-gate-conformance.test.js` each assert the new sentence and fail when it is removed.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Clarify that a pre-existing defect in a file the build touches goes through the deferral gate's fix-now test, so "pre-existing" alone no longer defers it.

## Technical Approach

Two prose additions plus the tests that pin them. The quoted Working Approach sentences in the build paragraph are pinned byte-for-byte against the init template and this repo's CLAUDE.md, so the new composition sentence goes after the quote and next to the existing routing clause ("A follow-up an implementer reports is this skill's to route..."), never inside it. The new deferral-gate bullet follows the existing "Out of scope of this plan / spec" bullet, which already states the in-diff rule.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — add the composition sentence after the quoted Working Approach text in "Scope and edit discipline"
- `plugin/skills/_shared/deferral-gate.md` — add the "pre-existing alone is not a defer reason" bullet to Bad reasons to skip a fix
- `tests/working-approach-scope-discipline.test.js` — pin the new build sentence
- `tests/deferral-gate-conformance.test.js` — pin the new gate bullet

## Gotchas

- `tests/working-approach-scope-discipline.test.js` pins the three quoted sentences against `plugin/skills/init/claude-md-template.md` and this repo's `CLAUDE.md` (Update Mode's conformance checker). Editing inside the quote breaks byte-conformance, so the new sentence must sit outside it.
- Do not change `DEFER_REASONS` or the `pre-existing-outside-diff` definition. The defect is that the reason was misapplied, not that the vocabulary is wrong.

## Original request

build / deferral-gate: the quoted surgical-changes rule and the deferral gate disagree on a pre-existing defect in an in-diff file

**Summary:** `/build` tells every implementer that a pre-existing bug is "a follow-up to report, not a fix to fold in". `_shared/deferral-gate.md` says a file in the build's diff is in scope. Neither says how the two compose, so agents in one run applied both.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `skills/build/SKILL.md` ("Scope and edit discipline", the quoted Working Approach sentence) and `skills/_shared/deferral-gate.md` (the bad-reasons list and the `pre-existing-outside-diff` definition)

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `/flow` on a record whose diff touches a file that already contains an unrelated, pre-existing defect.
2. Let a reviewer or hindsight agent notice that defect during `/review`.
3. Watch how it is dispositioned in `/review` and `/polish`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: one rule decides. The surgical rule binds the implementer mid-task (report it, don't widen the task). Once the defect is reported, routing runs the deferral gate's fix-now test. "Pre-existing" is never enough on its own to defer a defect in an in-diff file.
Actual: a review agent classified a pre-existing mismatch in two in-diff files as `pre-existing-outside-diff`, a reason the gate reserves for files the diff does not touch. It wrote that the parent should choose which rule governs, and the controller had to rule (it applied the gate and fixed the mismatch). Later phases in the same run deferred five similar in-diff items citing only "pre-existing", which the gate does not accept as a reason.

**Definition:** Clear

**Suggested fix:** add one sentence to both places. In `build/SKILL.md`: the quoted rule limits what an implementer changes mid-task; it does not decide the reported follow-up's disposition. In `deferral-gate.md`: a reported pre-existing defect in an in-diff file goes through the fix-now test like any other finding, and "pre-existing" alone is not a defer reason.

**Plugin version:** 6.138.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build` runs every check in `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` before finalizing a plan (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:130`: "one bold paragraph per check; the file, not this sentence, is the list"). The file holds 24 bold-paragraph checks (24,601 bytes, well under the 45 KB per-file ceiling in `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js:31`).

The closest existing rule is the **Consumer-enumeration check** (`plan-authoring-checks.md:51`, from #2594). It fires only "when a plan task changes which rows of a shared table or frame a reader returns". It then enumerates every consumer of that reader and classifies each as pick-one or list-all. No check covers a task that gives an **existing function a new external dependency or side effect**: a store or network read, a new pipeline stage, a new environment requirement. In that case every test that calls the function, in any test module, needs the same stub or fixture.

The observed failure (original request below): a plan task added a configuration-store read to an export job's existing `run()`. The plan stubbed the read only in `run()`'s own test module. Two CI-allowlisted cases in another test module also call `run()`; with the change they reached the real store and failed. Every per-task review passed, because each compares its own diff against its own brief. Only the whole-branch review's focused test run caught it, at the cost of one Critical finding, one fix-wave item and a ~30-minute local re-run.

## Deliverables

1. Add one new bold-paragraph check to `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`, placed directly after the Consumer-enumeration check: **Dependency-caller enumeration check (extends the Consumer-enumeration check)**. It must state:
   - **Trigger:** a plan task adds an external dependency or side effect to an existing function (a store, network or filesystem read, a new stage or subprocess, a new required environment variable or config key).
   - **Action:** grep every test directory in the repo, not only the function's own test module, for callers of that function. List each caller module in the task's Files block (`Modify:`/`Test:`) together with the stub or fixture that caller needs.
   - **Why:** a per-task review compares the task's diff against its own brief, so an unlisted caller module in another test file passes every task review and fails only at the whole-branch review or in CI. Use the incident above as the archetype, in the file's existing one-sentence-archetype style, with no project names.
   - **Check B hook:** `Scope keywords:` can name the function, so `plan-audit.js` Check B's fs-walk surfaces caller test files the plan's task list omitted. This mirrors the Consumer-enumeration check's closing sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `plan-authoring-checks.md` contains a bold paragraph headed `Dependency-caller enumeration check` immediately after the Consumer-enumeration check paragraph.
- The paragraph names the trigger (a new external dependency or side effect on an existing function, with the store, network or filesystem read, new stage, and new environment requirement examples).
- The paragraph requires grepping every test directory for callers and listing each caller module, with its stub or fixture, in the task's Files block.
- The paragraph names `Scope keywords:` as the Check B hook for surfacing omitted caller files.
- The Consumer-enumeration check paragraph itself is unchanged.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Add a plan-authoring check so a build plan that gives an existing function a new dependency also lists every test that calls it, before any task runs.

## Technical Approach

A prose-only, one-paragraph addition to a single file. It extends the existing Consumer-enumeration check by analogy rather than widening that check's trigger. That keeps the two failure classes distinct: changed return rows need consumer classification, while a new dependency needs a stub in every caller. Following the file's convention, each check is one self-contained bold paragraph with a trigger, an action, a why, and an archetype. `SKILL.md:130` treats the file as the list, so no other file restates the checks.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — new Dependency-caller enumeration check paragraph after the Consumer-enumeration check

## Gotchas

- Indirect callers matter. A test that calls a wrapper around the changed function hits the same dependency. A one-level grep for the function's own name misses them. The paragraph should tell the author to follow wrappers one level up, or to name the affected test command, so the gap surfaces at authoring time.
- Keep the archetype project-neutral, matching the file's existing archetypes: describe "an export job's entry point" and "a configuration-store read", not the reporting project's own module names.

## Original request

build/plan-authoring-checks: enumerate every test caller when a task adds a dependency to an existing function

**Summary:** The plan-authoring checks have no rule for a task that gives an existing function a new external dependency. A test module the plan never listed breaks, and only the whole-branch review catches it.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` (Consumer-enumeration check)

**Use case:** A plan task gave an existing entry-point function (an export job's `run()`) a new external dependency: a configuration-store read on every call. The plan stubbed that read in the function's own test module only. Two cases in another test module also call `run()`; both are in the project's CI allowlist. With the change they reached the real store and failed, so the CI Python job would have gone red.

Every per-task review passed, because each compares its own diff against its own brief. Only the whole-branch review's focused test run caught it, at the cost of one Critical finding, one fix-wave item and one ~30-minute local Spark re-run.

The Consumer-enumeration check (#2594) covers a reader whose returned rows change. It does not cover a function that gains a new external dependency or side effect, where every test calling the function, in any module, needs the same stub. Proposed: when a plan task adds an external dependency or side effect to an existing function (a store or network read, a new stage, a new environment requirement), the plan greps `tests/` for every caller across all modules. It then lists each caller module in the task's Files block, together with the stub or fixture that caller needs.

**Definition:** Clear

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build`'s Common Step 1.5 audits the plan before SDD dispatch with `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/plan-audit.js" {plan-file}` (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:182`, procedure in `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md`). The CLI takes only a plan file (`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/args.js` `USAGE`: `plan-audit.js <plan-file> [--repo-root <dir>] [--count-tasks] [--bytes]`). It never reads the spec.

Its five checks (`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`) are Check A (plan `Files:` paths exist, `checkA` at line 54, returning `{ ok, missing, missingDetail }`), Check B (scope-keyword sweep), Check C (verification-command pre-check), Check D (control-byte scan), and the headroom check. **None of them compares the plan against the spec's Acceptance Criteria.** The original request says Check A "matches the plan against the spec's Deliverables and cites acceptance criteria only by number". That attribution does not match the code: Check A only checks that file paths exist, so its `ok: true, missing: []` meant "every planned path exists", not "every criterion is covered".

Today, plan-to-spec coverage is checked only by prose judgment:

- `/superpowers:writing-plans`' own self-review, a third-party step, and the `Spec coverage` self-review line in `plugin/skills/build/micro-plan.md:67` for fast-lane micro-plans.
- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`'s instruction to forward the spec's `## Acceptance Criteria` excerpt into every per-task review.

The observed failure (original request below): one numbered acceptance criterion carried three clauses separated by sentences and semicolons. The plan covered two of them. The dropped clause was a counting invariant and the only test guarding an assumption a correctness proof rested on. plan-audit passed. Only the whole-branch review caught the gap, costing one extra fix dispatch and a scoped re-review that a pre-dispatch check could have saved.

## Deliverables

1. **New check, Check E (acceptance-criterion clause coverage), in `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`.** Given the spec's `## Acceptance Criteria` section and the plan text:
   - Split each criterion (a numbered item or a `-` bullet) into clauses on sentence boundaries and `;`.
   - Give each clause a stable id, `AC{item}.{clause}` (1-based).
   - Report a clause as covered when the plan names its id, or quotes its text, in a task's test step or in a spec-coverage map row. Report it as waived when the plan carries a line `Waived AC{item}.{clause}: {reason}`.
   - Return `{ ok: true, uncovered: [{id, clause}], waived: [{id, reason}], unparsed: [{item, raw}] }`. Check E is warn-only: `ok` is always `true`, so the CLI exit code is unchanged.
2. **A distinguishable could-not-parse signal**, per the repo's `parse-signal-discipline` project skill. A spec with no `## Acceptance Criteria` section, or a criterion item the splitter cannot break into clauses, lands in `unparsed`. It is never silently reported as "fully covered".
3. **CLI input:** add an optional `--spec <path>` flag to `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/args.js` and `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js`. Check E runs only when `--spec` is given. Without it, the envelope's `checkE` reads `{ ok: true, skipped: 'no-spec' }`. The existing call shapes (`--count-tasks`, `--bytes`, plain audit) keep working unchanged.
4. **Build wiring (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` Common Step 1.5 and `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md`):** pass `--spec {run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md` (the materialized spec) when one exists. Document Check E in "What each check covers" and in Result interpretation. A non-empty `uncovered` means the plan author amends the plan before dispatch, either naming each clause id in a task's test step or adding a `Waived` line. Under auto mode this happens without a prompt and is logged via `log-decision.js`. A non-empty `unparsed` is surfaced as a warning and logged, never treated as covered.
5. **Plan-authoring rule (`plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`):** one paragraph telling the plan author to cite `AC{item}.{clause}` ids in each task's test step (or a spec-coverage map table), so Check E can match coverage by id rather than by fuzzy text.
6. **Tests** under `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/`: `checks.test.js` cases for full coverage, one dropped clause (the original incident's shape: three clauses in one numbered item, two covered), a waived clause, and an unparseable criterion. `parser.test.js`/`cli.test.js` cases for `--spec` and the `skipped: 'no-spec'` envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `plan-audit.js {plan} --spec {spec}` on a spec whose AC item 2 has three clauses, against a plan citing only `AC2.1` and `AC2.2`, reports `checkE.uncovered` containing `AC2.3` with that clause's text.
- The same plan with a `Waived AC2.3: {reason}` line reports `AC2.3` under `waived`, not `uncovered`.
- A spec with no `## Acceptance Criteria` section yields a non-empty `checkE.unparsed`, not an empty `uncovered` list.
- Without `--spec`, the JSON envelope carries `checkE: { ok: true, skipped: 'no-spec' }`, and the exit code and every other check's output match the current behavior.
- Check E never sets `ok: false`. A plan with uncovered clauses still exits `0` when Checks A-D and headroom pass.
- `build/plan-audit.md` documents Check E's coverage rule, its waiver line, and its Result-interpretation handling. `build/SKILL.md` Common Step 1.5 passes `--spec` when the materialized spec exists.
- `build/plan-authoring-checks.md` tells plan authors to cite `AC{item}.{clause}` ids.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Add a plan-audit check that warns before a build starts when the plan leaves a clause of an acceptance criterion uncovered.

## Technical Approach

Add a pure `checkE(specText, planText)` to `checks.js`, next to the existing checks and following their `{ok, ...}` envelope convention. Add clause splitting to `parser.js`, keeping one parser module. Thread `--spec` through `args.js` and `plan-audit.js` the same way `--repo-root` is threaded. Make Check E warn-only rather than a stop: clause splitting is a prose heuristic, and a hard gate on a heuristic would block builds on false positives. The incident's cost was one fix dispatch, so a pre-dispatch warning that prompts a plan amendment is proportionate. Use id citation (`AC{item}.{clause}`) as the primary match, so coverage does not depend on fuzzy text similarity. Quoted clause text is accepted as a fallback.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js` — new `checkE`
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js` — Acceptance Criteria clause splitter
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/args.js` — `--spec <path>` flag and `USAGE`
- `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — read the spec file and add `checkE` to the envelope
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` — Invocation, Result interpretation, What each check covers
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — Common Step 1.5 invocation passes `--spec`
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — AC clause-id citation rule
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/checks.test.js` — Check E cases
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` — clause-splitter cases
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/cli.test.js` — `--spec` and `skipped: 'no-spec'` envelope cases

## Gotchas

- Splitting on `;` and sentence ends will mis-split clauses that contain inline code with semicolons or abbreviations ("e.g."). Strip code spans before splitting. Prefer reporting an item as `unparsed` over guessing.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: plans written by `/superpowers:writing-plans` often carry a "Spec coverage map" table, per the original request. Plans are deleted after a build, so this checkout cannot confirm it. Confirm by reading the current upstream writing-plans template before relying on the table as a coverage source.
- `/superpowers:writing-plans` is third-party, so its template cannot be changed here. The id-citation rule reaches plan authors only through `plan-authoring-checks.md`, which `/build` already hands to plan authoring.
- The micro-plan path (`micro-plan.md`, fast-lane) skips `plan-audit.js` entirely. Check E does not apply there by construction, the same as Check D's documented exception.
- `plan-audit.md` lists Check A/B/C and headroom as sharing one skip gate. Decide explicitly whether Check E shares that gate. It reads only text already in memory, like Check D, so running it on the skip path too is defensible. Record the ruling in `plan-audit.md`.

## Original request

plan-audit: Check A passes a plan that drops one clause of a multi-clause acceptance criterion

**Summary:** plan-audit's coverage check passes a plan that drops one clause of a multi-clause acceptance criterion.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/plan-audit.js` (Check A, run by `/claude-tweaks:build` before SDD dispatch)

**Use case:**
- **What was dropped:** a spec's acceptance criterion carried three clauses in one numbered item, separated by sentences and semicolons. The written plan covered two of them. The missing clause was a counting invariant (an entity with several instances counts once per recipient). That clause was the only test guarding an assumption a correctness proof rested on.
- **Why plan-audit missed it:** Check A reported `ok: true, missing: []`. It matches the plan against the spec's Deliverables and cites acceptance criteria only by number, so the criterion counted as covered once any task cited its number.
- **How it surfaced:** the whole-branch review after all tasks were built caught the gap as its one Important finding. That cost one extra fix dispatch and a scoped re-review, work a pre-dispatch check could have saved.

**Suggested direction:** a per-clause coverage check.
- Split each numbered acceptance criterion into clauses (sentences, `;`).
- Require every clause to be named by some task's test step, or waived by an explicit plan ruling.
- Report uncovered clauses as Check A warnings, quoting the clause text.

Many plans already carry a "Spec coverage map" table, which the check could read.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.138.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2702, #2767, #2776, #3088

## Current State

Record #3074 (merged as `666d97af5`) replaced `hooks.json`'s per-pattern `if` entries with one unconditional Bash handler per tool-use event, plus a command-word prefilter in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/bash-prefilter.js`. Every Bash call now spawns `bin/hooks.js` once per event regardless.

Bare shell redirection (`echo x > file`, `cmd >> file`) still has no gate coverage:

- `fileWriteTargets` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` returns early unless `t[0]` is in `WRITE_SHAPES`, and no branch reads a redirection target. Its header comment lists bare redirection as "Still NOT covered, and deliberately".
- The prefilter can't reach it either. `bash-prefilter.js`'s `SEPARATORS` (`/[\s;&|()<>\`{}=]+/`) splits `<`/`>` away as separators, and no command word marks a redirection, so `echo x > tracked.js` takes the skip path and the full handler never loads.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md`'s "Bare shell redirection" bullet records it as declined on the measured marginal cost: full handler minus skip path, about 49 ms idle and 54 ms under contention (best-of-30, this repo's Windows box).

The old rationale (an unconditional matcher's per-call spawn cost) no longer applies, since the spawn happens anyway. The other two gaps #3074's spec named, path-qualified git and `env`-wrapped git, are now covered end to end, so redirection is the one write shape left uncovered.

## Deliverables

1. **Parser.** Add redirection-target resolution to `git-command.js`, either as a `redirectTargets(command, cwd)` sibling or as a pre-pass inside `fileWriteTargets`. It resolves `>`, `>>`, `&>`, `&>>`, `>|` and fd-prefixed `N>`/`N>>` targets per shell segment, whether the operator is spaced (`> f`) or glued (`>f`). It runs regardless of `t[0]`, so `echo`, `printf`, `cat`, a bare `> f`, and a redirect on any other command are all reached. Use the same fail-closed posture as the other write shapes: an unresolvable target (`$VAR`, a backtick or `$(…)`, process substitution `>(…)`) resolves to no target, never a guess. An fd duplication (`>&2`, `2>&1`) is not a file target.
2. **Prefilter reach.** In `shouldRunFull` (`bash-prefilter.js`), run the full handler when the command holds an unquoted output redirection whose target is not an fd duplication (`>&N`) or a `DEVNULL_LIKE` sink (`/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`). `2>&1` and `> /dev/null` are the most common redirections an agent writes, so keeping them on the skip path is what keeps the added cost off most redirecting calls. Measure the skip-path cost after the change and re-record the figure in `policy-schema-coverage.md`.
3. **Gate wiring.** Feed the redirection targets into `checkWorktreeRequired`'s `writeTargetPaths` (`pre-tool-use.js`) as `exemptible: true`, so the existing exemptions apply unchanged: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/`, a gitignored target, and `DEVNULL_LIKE`. Feed them into the pipeline-shadow guard's candidate list too (the `fileWriteTargets`/`mkdirTargets` loop near the `pipelinesDir` check), since a redirect can create a shadow run dir just as `tee` can.
4. **Coverage contract.** Add a `- Bash redirections:` line to `policy-schema-coverage.md`'s gate coverage block, with a matching `GATE_COVERAGE` field in `pre-tool-use.js`. Pin the pair in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` the way `bashWriteShapes` is pinned. Move the "Bare shell redirection" bullet from declined to covered, and remove the "Still NOT covered" redirection line from `git-command.js`'s header comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo x > tracked-file.js`, `printf y >> tracked-file.js`, and `cat a > tracked-file.js` issued from a `worktree-always` main checkout are DENIED, with the same remediation message as `cp`/`tee`.
- `echo x > /dev/null`, `cmd 2>&1`, `cmd > ignored.log` where `ignored.log` is gitignored, and `echo x > .claude-tweaks/pipelines/<run>/x` are ALLOWED.
- `cmd 2>&1` and `cmd > /dev/null` with no other covered word take the prefilter's skip path, which the e2e `require.cache` probe in `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js` shows by loading no heavy module.
- `echo x > "$OUT"` and `echo x > $(mktemp)` resolve to no target and are ALLOWED, the same fail-closed posture as the other write shapes.
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` pins the new coverage line against its code twin, and the prose and the code agree.
- `perf/hooks-prefilter.test.js` still passes. `npm test` adds no failures attributable to this change against the Windows baseline.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate now also catches file writes made by plain shell redirection (`> file`, `>> file`) from the main checkout.

## Technical Approach

`splitSegments` already gives per-segment strings with quotes respected, and it doesn't split on `>`, so a redirection stays inside its segment. Inside `forEachCommandSegment`'s handler, scan the token list (from `tokenize`, which keeps quoted spans whole) for redirection operators:

- **Standalone operator.** A token equal to `>`, `>>`, `>|`, `&>` or `&>>`, or matching `^\d+>>?$`, takes the next token as its target.
- **Glued operator.** A token like `>file`, `2>>log` or `&>out` is split at the operator.
- **Not file targets.** A token like `>&2` or `2>&1` is an fd duplication. A target starting with `(` is process substitution.

Each target goes through the existing `resolveWriteTarget(effCwd, raw)`, which already applies `isUnresolvable` and the `DEVNULL_LIKE` check, and emits `{ action: 'write', file }`. Because this scan runs before the `WRITE_SHAPES.includes(t[0])` early return (or in its own sibling), the command word doesn't matter.

For the prefilter, add a small `hasFileRedirection(command)` to `bash-prefilter.js`. It walks the raw command once with the same single-quote, double-quote and backslash state machine `splitSegments` uses, but no heavy requires. It returns true at the first unquoted `>` whose operator and target, read the same way as above, are neither an fd duplication nor a `DEVNULL_LIKE` path. `shouldRunFull` ORs it with the word scan and the assignment-plus-`$` rule. Keep the prefilter a superset of what the parser can resolve: when the prefilter can't tell (an odd quoting shape, say), it returns true and fails open to the full handler, which is the existing rule.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`: the redirection-target scan (`redirectTargets` or inside `fileWriteTargets`), plus the header comment update.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/bash-prefilter.js`: `hasFileRedirection` and its use in `shouldRunFull`, plus the header comment update.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`: redirection targets into `checkWorktreeRequired`'s `writeTargetPaths` and the pipeline-shadow candidate list, plus a new `GATE_COVERAGE` field.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md`: a new coverage-block line, the bare-redirection bullet moved to covered, and the re-measured cost.
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`: pin the new coverage line against `GATE_COVERAGE`.
- `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js`: run/skip unit cases for redirection shapes, plus e2e deny and allow cases.
- `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js`: the deny and allow acceptance cases, if the e2e tests live here rather than in the prefilter suite.
- `perf/hooks-prefilter.test.js`: confirm the ratio budget still holds. Add a redirect-bearing skip sample only if the measurement shows `2>&1` costs anything.
- `docs/hooks.md`: one clause on the Bash prefilter bullet saying redirection is reached.

## Gotchas

- `2>&1`, `>&2` and `> /dev/null` are in a large share of the Bash calls agents issue. If the prefilter sends them to the full handler, the ~50 ms marginal cost lands on most calls, which is the cost this record was declined over. Keeping them on the skip path is load-bearing.
- A `>` inside quotes (`echo "a > b"`), inside a heredoc body, or inside a `[[ a > b ]]` string comparison is not a redirection. The parser must not fabricate a target from it. A heredoc body sits on its own lines after `<<EOF`, and `splitSegments` treats the newline as a segment break, so heredoc lines can show up as their own segments. Treat a target the parser can't prove as "no target", the same rule `gitTargets` follows.
- `>(…)` process substitution and `<` input redirection are not write targets.
- `noclobber`'s `>|` is still a write.
- The gate's remediation text for write shapes names the command. Check that the deny message reads sensibly when the "command" is a redirection.
- `tee` is already covered. `cmd | tee f` should keep producing exactly one target, not a duplicate.

## Original request

Gate bare shell redirection (> / >>) under worktree-always now that every Bash call reaches the hook

Origin: wrap-up leftover from #3074 (spec Deliverable 8)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Record #3074 replaced hooks.json's per-pattern `if` entries with one unconditional Bash handler per tool-use event, plus a command-word prefilter in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/bash-prefilter.js`. Every Bash call now spawns `bin/hooks.js` once per event regardless. Bare shell redirection (`echo x > file`, `cmd >> file`) still has no gate coverage: `fileWriteTargets` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` recognizes no redirection target, and the prefilter has no command word to key on. `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md`'s bare-redirection bullet records it as declined on the measured marginal cost. That cost is the full handler minus the skip path, about 49 ms idle and 54 ms under contention (best-of-30, this repo's Windows box), and it would be paid by every redirecting Bash call. The old rationale (an unconditional matcher's per-call spawn cost) no longer applies. Path-qualified git and `env`-wrapped git, the other two gaps #3074's spec named, are now covered end to end, so only redirection remains.

## Deliverables

1. Teach `fileWriteTargets` (or a sibling `redirectTargets`) to resolve `>` / `>>` / `&>` / `>|` redirection targets per shell segment, with the same fail-closed posture as the other write shapes. Unresolvable targets (`$VAR`, process substitution) resolve to no target, never a guess.
2. Make the prefilter reach redirections: a `>` outside quotes runs the full handler. Measure the added skip-path cost, and re-record it in `policy-schema-coverage.md`.
3. Exempt the same paths the other write shapes exempt (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/`, gitignored targets, `/dev/null`-like sinks), and add redirection to the gate-coverage block plus its pinned test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo x > tracked-file.js` from a `worktree-always` main checkout is DENIED, with the same remediation message as `cp`/`tee`.
- `echo x > /dev/null`, `cmd 2>&1 | tee log` into a gitignored path, and `> .claude-tweaks/pipelines/<run>/x` are ALLOWED.
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`'s coverage block lists redirection, and the prose and the code twin agree.
- `perf/hooks-prefilter.test.js` still passes, and the redirection-reaching rule is in place.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate now also catches file writes made by plain shell redirection (`> file`, `>> file`) from the main checkout.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build` tells every implementer, in fixed words, that "scratch checks stay scratch" (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:223`, quoting CLAUDE.md's Working Approach). Nothing in build's plan guidance (`plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`) or its Final Verification step (`SKILL.md:266-272`, which runs `skills/test/verification.md`'s runner checks only) says what happens to the *result* of a scratch check. That matters when the check is the only evidence for an acceptance criterion. The plan is free to route that result into a conversational "build handoff" (`plugin/skills/build/handoff-template.md`).

That works in one session, but not under `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call split. Call 1 (`build,test`) and call 2 (`review,polish,wrap-up`) are separate Task calls that share only the run directory. Review's spec-compliance check marks each criterion `met`/`partially met`/`not met` by asking whether it is "verifiable from the code and tests" (`plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:31`). It has no place to look for a scratch result call 1 produced.

Observed (original request below): an AC of "a rendered contrast audit over the main routes reports 0 failures" was met by a scratch audit in call 1. `decisions.md` mentioned "the AC2 rendered audit" with no result, counts, or log path, so call 2 had to re-run the whole audit (68 page renders plus controls).

`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` is 45,186 bytes against the 46,080-byte per-SKILL.md ceiling (`plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js:31`, `45 * 1024`). New prose has to live in a sub-file.

## Deliverables

1. Add an "AC-evidence persistence" check to `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`. When a plan task verifies an acceptance criterion only with a scratch (uncommitted) check, the plan must name that check's run-dir evidence destination, never a conversational handoff. The destination is one `decisions.md` entry written via `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/log-decision.js" --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR" --status AUTO --step "AC evidence"`. Its text carries:
   - the criterion it covers;
   - the exact command shape;
   - the pass/fail counts.
   When the check's output is too long for one line, the plan also writes the full log to `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/evidence/` and cites that path in the same entry.
2. In `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md`'s Acceptance Criteria check (check 2), add: before marking a criterion `not met` for lack of code or test evidence, read the run's `decisions.md` for an `AC evidence` entry naming it. When one exists, cite it as the criterion's evidence instead of re-executing the check. When `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is unset (standalone review), behavior is unchanged.
3. Leave `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` unchanged. If a pointer is unavoidable, it must fit the ceiling headroom; confirm with `node plugin/bin/context-cost-report.js` or the context-cost test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `plan-authoring-checks.md` carries a check requiring a scratch-verified AC's result to go to the run dir via `log-decision.js --step "AC evidence"`, with the criterion, command shape, and pass/fail counts in the entry text, plus a `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/evidence/` log for long output.
- `review/code-mode-steps.md`'s check 2 instructs reading `decisions.md` for an `AC evidence` entry and citing it rather than re-running the check. It names the unset-`$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` standalone case as unchanged.
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` stays under the context-cost ceiling. The repo's context-cost test (`tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js`) passes.
- `npm test` passes, since conformance tests pin skill prose repo-wide.

## Release Note

Fix dispatched builds losing scratch-check results between calls: an acceptance criterion verified by an uncommitted check now leaves its result in the run directory for review to cite.

## Technical Approach

A prose-only change in two sub-files. The evidence channel reuses the existing sanctioned run-dir writer (`bin/log-decision.js`) rather than a new artifact format, so `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s console and any later reader see it in the same `decisions.md` they already read. Write the `evidence/` subdirectory only for long logs, and keep its path under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, never a relative path, per `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — new AC-evidence persistence check
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — check 2 reads `AC evidence` entries before declaring a criterion unverified
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — no change expected (ceiling headroom ~900 bytes)

## Gotchas

- "Scratch checks stay scratch" governs whether a check's *code* is committed, not whether its *result* is recorded. The new check must say so explicitly, so the two rules are not read as contradicting each other.
- A recorded result is evidence, not proof. Review may still re-run a check whose entry looks inconsistent with the diff, for example a stale command shape. The rule removes the forced re-run; it does not forbid one.
- Byte-pinned conformance tests cover `plugin/skills/**` prose. Run the full suite before merging, not just the targeted ones.

## Original request

build: an AC met only by a scratch check leaves no run-dir artifact for /dispatch's second call

**Summary:** An acceptance criterion met only by a scratch (uncommitted) check leaves no run-dir artifact, so /dispatch's second call cannot verify it without re-running the check.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** build (plan + test-phase exit), under /claude-tweaks:dispatch's two-call split

**Use case:**
A record's acceptance criterion read "a rendered contrast audit over the main routes reports 0 failures." The plan /build wrote said the audit "stays scratch (per the project's working approach); its result is reported in the build handoff." Under /dispatch's two-call split (`build,test`, then `review,polish,wrap-up` as a fresh Task call with no conversation), there is no conversational handoff. The first call's `decisions.md` mentioned "the AC2 rendered audit" but recorded no result, counts or log path. The second call's review has to re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts, so it had nothing to read for that criterion and had to re-run the whole audit (68 page renders plus controls).

Why was this possible? The plan routed the scratch check's result into a conversational handoff. Plans assume one session. Nothing in /build's plan or test-phase guidance says an AC verified only by an uncommitted check must persist its evidence to the run dir. CAUSAL: systemic.

Proposed fix: when an acceptance criterion's only evidence is a scratch check, /build's test-phase exit (or the plan template) should require one of two things:
- a `decisions.md` line carrying the result (pass/fail counts and the command shape), or
- the check's log written into the run dir.

The second dispatch call's review can then cite it as a raw artifact instead of re-running it or trusting a mention.

Acceptance: a dispatched two-call run whose AC is met by a scratch check leaves, in the run dir after call 1, a result line or log that call 2's review cites without re-executing the check.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.137.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

The original request says claude-tweaks "already ships a blast-radius mod that intercepts risky commands (rm -rf, git reset --hard, etc.) and asks Proceed/Cancel". The checkout does not support that premise:

- The only blast-radius code is `plugin/bin/blast-radius.js` (with `plugin/bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js`). It is the gather step of `assess-agent-autonomy`'s merge-check: merge-base resolution, diff numstat, and sensitive-path classification at merge time. It never intercepts a command.
- claude-tweaks ships no mods. Its tool-call interception is the PreToolUse hook (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`), and it only ever emits `permissionDecision: 'deny'` (pre-tool-use.js:422). It never emits an ask prompt, so no claude-tweaks gate can leave an unattended run waiting on a Proceed/Cancel.
- None of its gates targets `rm -rf` or `git reset --hard` (no match for either in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/`).
- Recursive deletion inside claude-tweaks' own unattended machinery runs through Node `fs.rmSync`, not a Bash `rm` command. Examples: `plugin/bin/lib/file-lock.js:115`, `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js:834`, `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js:132`. Shipped skill prose uses only single-file `rm -f` (for example `plugin/skills/_shared/headless-self-report.md:51`).

The external change: Claude Code 2.1.281+ times out a flagged dangerous `rm` prompt after two minutes in unattended, auto, or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` runs, denying the command with a rewrite hint instead of hanging (source in the original request below).

## Deliverables

1. A written comparison, posted as a comment on this record, of the native dangerous-`rm` timeout against what claude-tweaks actually ships. It should cover:
   - the premise correction above: no blast-radius command interceptor exists, and `blast-radius.js` is a merge-time gather;
   - whether any claude-tweaks PreToolUse gate overlaps or conflicts with the native prompt and timeout (expected answer: no, because the gates are deny-only and none targets `rm`);
   - whether any claude-tweaks unattended path (`/claude-tweaks:dispatch`, `/claude-tweaks:flow` auto, Routine firings, `reconcile`) issues a Bash command the native flag would trip, which would now be denied after two minutes rather than hanging;
   - where the "blast-radius mod" in the original request lives, if it exists outside this repo, so the comparison can be redirected there.
2. For any claude-tweaks path the comparison finds the native flag would trip, file a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body. Otherwise, state explicitly that no adjustment is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The comparison comment exists on this record and addresses each of the four points in Deliverable 1, citing the files above.
- It states a clear verdict: no claude-tweaks adjustment needed, or the specific path(s) that need one, each with a linked filed record.
- No claude-tweaks code changes land in this record.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of claude-tweaks' guardrails against Claude Code's native dangerous-rm timeout.

## Technical Approach

A desk comparison. Confirm the deny-only posture of `pre-tool-use.js` and the absence of Bash recursive-`rm` in shipped skill prose and `bin/` code with a repo-wide grep. Then read the native permission-modes documentation for the exact trigger set, which may cover more than `rm`, and re-check the unattended paths against that set.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/blast-radius.js` — the only blast-radius code; merge-time gather, not an interceptor
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — the PreToolUse gates; deny-only
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — representative unattended recursive deletion via `fs.rmSync`

## Gotchas

- The original request's premise of a shipped blast-radius mod is contradicted by the checkout. #3055 lists a "blast-radius-style guardrail" only as a candidate for a future mod. Do not build one under this record; that is #3055's evaluation.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the native flag fires only on Bash-tool commands, not on Node `fs.rmSync` inside a hook or CLI subprocess. Confirm from the permission-modes documentation.
- The native trigger set may widen across Claude Code versions. Cite the version the comparison was made against.

## Original request

Compare blast-radius against Claude Code's native dangerous-rm timeout

Current State:
- Claude Code (2.1.281+) now times out a flagged dangerous rm prompt after two minutes in unattended/auto/--dangerously-skip-permissions runs, denying the command with a rewrite hint instead of hanging.
- claude-tweaks already ships a blast-radius mod that intercepts risky commands (rm -rf, git reset --hard, etc.) and asks Proceed/Cancel.

Deliverables:
- Check whether blast-radius's own unattended-run behavior overlaps or conflicts with this native timeout.
- Align blast-radius's timeout/denial behavior with the native one where it makes sense, or document why it intentionally differs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A written comparison of the two behaviors.
- Any needed blast-radius adjustment made or explicitly deferred with a reason.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#critical-paths

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review`'s Step 3 dispatches each lens as a reproduction pair at `medium` effort and above (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md:39`, 3f Test Quality included). `categoriseReproduction` (`plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js:285`, CLI `plugin/bin/review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction`) confirms a finding only when both agents report it at the same location: `sameLocation` with `LINE_TOLERANCE_REPRODUCTION` (exact path, line ±2), then a substance check. Findings with no same-location partner land `unconfirmed`.

The dispatch prompt already carries one anchoring instruction outside the byte-identical Calibration/Output block: `Path:Line` must be file-native, never bundle-relative (`step3-lens-dispatch.md:74`). It has no rule for where a coverage finding is anchored. The 3f checklist (`step3-lens-dispatch.md:205-214`) asks about missing edge-case and error-path tests and weak tests, so the same coverage gap can legitimately be anchored at the test file or at the production line.

Observed (reporter, plugin 6.136.0, `medium` effort): both 3f agents found the same gap ("production guard X is only pinned by a Spark-gated test, so CI never exercises it"). One anchored it at the test's decorator line, the other at the unguarded production line, so neither reproduced. All six 3a/3f findings landed `unconfirmed` and were confirmed only through the reviewer's direct-verification override.

## Deliverables

1. Add a coverage-finding anchor rule to `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s dispatch-prompt instructions, next to the file-native `Path:Line` rule at `:74` and outside the byte-identical Calibration/Output-template block. A missing-or-weak-test finding is anchored at the production line the test should pin, never at the test file. A finding about a test's own defect (refactor-coupled, non-discriminating, polluting) stays anchored at the test.
2. Restate the rule as one bullet in the 3f Test Quality checklist (`step3-lens-dispatch.md:205`) so the lens agent sees it where coverage questions are asked.
3. Leave `categoriseReproduction`'s matching unchanged (see Gotchas).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `step3-lens-dispatch.md` states the coverage anchor rule in the dispatch-prompt instructions, with both halves: coverage gap → production line; test-quality defect → test line.
- The 3f checklist carries the same rule as a bullet.
- The byte-identical Calibration/Output-template block is unchanged, so any conformance test pinning it to `_shared/criteria-review-quality.md` still passes.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Make review's test-quality agents anchor coverage findings at the code under test, so two agents finding the same gap now confirm each other.

## Technical Approach

A prompt-side rule fixes the cause: the two agents disagree on where to anchor, not on what they found. The reporter's optional matcher relaxation (treat a test-file finding whose evidence names the other side's `path:line` as same-location) was considered and not adopted here. It loosens a deterministic matcher on free-text evidence, which raises the risk of confirming coincidental pairs, the failure mode `categoriseReproduction`'s #1980 substance check exists to prevent. If anchor drift still shows up in practice after this rule ships, the matcher change can be revisited with that evidence.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — coverage anchor rule in the dispatch-prompt instructions and the 3f checklist

## Gotchas

- Keep the rule out of the byte-identical Calibration/Output-template block (`step3-lens-dispatch.md:107` onward). That block is the canonical copy of `_shared/criteria-review-quality.md` and must stay byte-identical.
- The reporter's second unconfirmed pair (same location, different wording) is a substance-match question, not an anchor question. This rule does not address it.
- The rule must be phrased so a lens agent can apply it without seeing sibling files. Dispatched agents only see their prompt.

## Original request

review: reproduction pairs anchor the same coverage gap at the test vs the code, so neither reproduces

**Component:** claude-tweaks `skills/review` (step3-lens-dispatch.md lens prompt, `bin/review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction`)
**Kind:** gap

## What happened

At `medium` review effort, both agents of the 3f (Test Quality) reproduction pair independently found the same issue — "the production guard X is only pinned by a Spark-gated test, so CI never exercises it" — but anchored it at different `Path:Line`s: one at the gated test's decorator line in the test file, the other at the unguarded production line it should pin. `categorise-reproduction` matches on `path` exact + `line ±2`, so both entries came back `unconfirmed`, as did a second shared finding where the agents wrote different wording. All six 3a/3f findings landed `unconfirmed` and were only confirmed through the reviewer's direct-verification override.

## Expected

Two agents that found the same coverage gap should reproduce it.

## Suggested fix

In the canonical lens prompt (3f especially), state the anchor rule for coverage findings: anchor a missing-or-weak-test finding at the production line the test should pin, never at the test. Optionally let `categorise-reproduction` treat a finding pair as same-location when one side's `path` is a test file whose evidence names the other side's `path:line`.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3047

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:test`'s pipeline path with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:70`) selects QA stories by `source_files` ∩ `node bin/verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}`. `--changed-files` (`plugin/bin/verify.js:156`, `changedFilesMode`) resolves its base through `resolveBase` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js:54`) with this precedence: `--base` first, then the checkout's own verification-stamp anchor whenever it is usable and not equal to HEAD (`:62-77`), and only then the `--integration-branch` merge-base (`:78-84`).

In a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the stamp. Bookkeeping commits follow (for example `/stories` committing a new story YAML), so by the time `/test` selects stories the stamp anchor is an ancestor of HEAD but not HEAD. The changed-file set is then only the post-stamp bookkeeping, never the build's own source changes. Observed (reporter, plugin 6.136.0): the set was a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in it, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components. The reporter selected stories by hand against `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`.

The stamp anchor is the right base for re-running tests (`affected`, `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table): the stamp records what was already verified. It is the wrong base for QA story selection, because the stamp says nothing about QA. `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md:9` reads the same `--changed-files` set to decide which files the design CLI gate judges, so it has the same blind spot.

## Deliverables

1. Add an opt-in `--ignore-stamp` flag to `verify.js --changed-files` (parsed in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js`, honored by `changedFilesMode`/`resolveBase`). It skips the stamp anchor and resolves the base from `--base` or the `--integration-branch` merge-base, keeping the existing exit-1 and `warning: resolved base equals HEAD` semantics. Reject it outside `--changed-files` the way the other read-only flags are rejected.
2. Switch `test/SKILL.md`'s pipeline QA story selection (`:70`) to `verify.js --changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}`, so selection compares story `source_files` against the run's own branch diff.
3. Switch `test/design-gate.md:9`'s `<changed-files>` resolution to the same `--ignore-stamp` form.
4. Leave `/claude-tweaks:test affected` (test re-runs) and `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping unchanged — they keep the stamp-anchored set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stamp anchored at commit A, a later source commit B, and a bookkeeping commit C on HEAD, `verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}` still returns only C's files, and `--changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}` returns B's and C's files (the merge-base diff). Both cases are covered in `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` and/or `cli.test.js`.
- `--ignore-stamp` with no resolvable `--base`/`--integration-branch` base exits 1 with a message, never an empty list.
- `--ignore-stamp` combined with a non-`--changed-files` mode is a usage error (exit 2), covered by `args.test.js`.
- `test/SKILL.md`'s QA selection and `design-gate.md` both name the `--ignore-stamp` form; the `affected` mode does not.
- The existing `verify` suites (`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/*.test.js`) pass.

## Release Note

Select pipeline QA stories against the run's full branch diff, so a build's own UI changes are never skipped because a verification stamp was written before them.

## Technical Approach

An additive flag keeps every existing `--changed-files` caller's behavior unchanged. Flipping the default would change the `affected`/`--scope` semantics that rely on the stamp anchor. The alternative of passing `--base $(git merge-base …)` from the skill prose was rejected: that hand-rolls merge-base resolution (`preferOriginRef`, degenerate-base handling) that `resolveBase` already owns.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — parse and validate `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — pass the flag through `changedFilesMode`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` — `resolveBase` skips the stamp anchor when asked
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — QA story selection uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md` — design-gate changed-file set uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` — stamp-anchored vs ignore-stamp base cases
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/args.test.js` — flag validation

## Gotchas

- `verify.js`'s usage string (`args.js:14`) and `verification.md`'s `--changed-files` description must name the new flag. Grep for every `--changed-files` mention in `plugin/skills/` before finishing (`test/SKILL.md`, `test/design-gate.md`, `test/verification.md`).
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/snippet-conformance.test.js` does not currently pin the `--changed-files` snippet. Run the full `npm test` anyway, because other conformance suites pin `test/SKILL.md` prose repo-wide.
- The reporter's alternative base (the run's materialize commit's parent) was not chosen. The integration-branch merge-base is already resolvable by `verify.js` without run-dir knowledge, and on a pr-first branch it is the same diff.

## Original request

test: pipeline QA story selection reads only post-stamp changes, so it can skip the build's own UI change

**Component:** claude-tweaks `skills/test` (pipeline QA selection) + `bin/verify.js --changed-files`
**Kind:** gap

## What happened

Inside a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the verification pass stamp. `/stories` then commits a new story YAML, and `/test` (with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present) selects stories by `source_files ∩ verify.js --changed-files`. Because `--changed-files` resolves its base to the stamp's `fullSha` whenever that sha is an ancestor of HEAD, the set at that point is only the post-stamp commits — here a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in that one-file set, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components.

## Expected

The pipeline's QA selection should compare story `source_files` against the run's own change set (the branch diff from its merge-base / the run's materialize base), not against "changes since the last verification stamp", which in a pipeline is almost always just the bookkeeping that follows `/build`.

## Workaround used

Selected stories manually against the branch diff (`git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`) and logged the deviation to `decisions.md`.

## Suggested fix

Give `/test`'s pipeline selection its own base (the run's materialize commit's parent, or `--integration-branch` merge-base) instead of the stamp-anchored `--changed-files`, or add a `--since-base` mode to `verify.js --changed-files` that ignores the stamp.


_Filed from a recommender-system `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` run (record #1207, plugin 6.136.0)._

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3048

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review`'s Step 6.7 (Late Findings Routing, `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:327`) consolidates the actionable findings from Steps 6, 6.5, 6.6, 6.65 and 6.66 into one table. Under a pipeline run it routes each finding by the resolved `review-auto-apply-ceiling` (`code-mode-steps.md:340`, `step3-routing.md`'s ceiling-keyed table). At `medium`, Low and Medium findings auto-apply as fix commits (`_shared/policy-schema.md:192`). Step 6.7 then folds each finding into its Step 7 summary section (`code-mode-steps.md:343`). It runs no QA story re-run, and nothing records that QA ran before those fixes.

`/claude-tweaks:test` ran the record's QA stories earlier in the pipeline. The QA line in `review-summary-template.md:53-61` (`### QA Validation (from /test)`, statuses ALL PASSED / PASSED WITH OBSERVATIONS / …) reports that earlier result with no freshness qualifier. The infrastructure to re-run only affected stories already exists. `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected` (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:44`) selects stories whose `source_files` intersect `verify.js --changed-files`, and stories carry a mandatory `source_files` array (`plugin/skills/stories/source-aware-design.md:66`).

Observed (reporter, 6.136.0): a single-record `auto` `/flow` run on a web UI record with `review-auto-apply-ceiling: medium`. Step 6.5 returned nine low/medium design findings, and Step 6.7 auto-applied them as nine commits that changed behaviour the passing stories describe (tooltip placement, focus/scroll after paging, a new pending state). One story's `verify` text was edited by the wave. Types/lint/tests/e2e were re-verified, but the QA stories were not re-run. The summary still read "QA: all passed" for a UI ten commits old, and the controller re-ran the stories by hand.

## Deliverables

1. In `code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7, after the resolved fixes are applied: when any applied fix touched a file listed in a QA story's `source_files`, re-run those stories via `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected` (scoped to the fix wave's changed files), and fold the result into the Step 7 QA line.
2. In `review-summary-template.md`'s QA Validation section, add a freshness qualifier for the case where QA was not re-run after an applied fix wave touching story `source_files` (for example when no dev server or browser is available): `{status} — ran before the review's fix wave ({N} commits since); stories touching changed files: {ids}`.
3. Apply the same rule to fixes applied interactively through Step 6.7's batch table ("Fix now"), not only auto-applied ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 names the post-wave re-run of affected QA stories via `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected`, gated on an applied fix touching any story's `source_files`.
- When no applied fix touches any story's `source_files`, Step 6.7 runs no QA re-run (no added cost for non-UI waves).
- `review-summary-template.md` documents the stale-QA qualifier and when it renders (applied wave touched story `source_files` and the re-run did not happen).
- The verdict comment's QA reporting reads the same qualified status (no separate wording).
- `code-mode-steps.md` stays under the per-file byte ceiling (`CEILING_BYTES`, `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js:31`), and `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Re-run affected QA stories after review auto-applies UI fixes, so the review summary never reports QA results for a UI that has since changed.

## Technical Approach

Prefer re-running over annotating. `test qa affected` already does the story selection, so the re-run reuses an existing mode instead of adding a new staleness mechanism. The qualifier only covers the case where a re-run cannot happen. The changed-file set for the wave is the files the Step 6.7 fix commits touched. Pass it the way `test/SKILL.md`'s `affected` mode documents (`verify.js --changed-files`), so stories untouched by the wave are not re-run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 post-wave affected-story re-run
- `plugin/skills/review/review-summary-template.md` — stale-QA qualifier on the QA Validation line

## Gotchas

- `code-mode-steps.md` is 41465 B against a 46080 B ceiling. Keep the Step 6.7 addition short, or cite a sub-file, as `focus-criterion-passes.md` already does for Steps 6.6-6.66.
- Out of scope: the reporter's related idea of running `design-wrapper review` before `/test`'s QA on web-surface records. That is a pipeline step-order change with its own cost tradeoff. File it separately if wanted.
- Step 3 Routing's own fix-now path (`code-mode-steps.md:258`) runs before Steps 4-7 and can also touch UI. This record is scoped to Step 6.7's late wave, the observed case.
- In a headless run with no dev server, the re-run self-skips. The qualifier must then render rather than silently reporting the pre-wave status.

## Original request

review Step 6.7: an auto-applied fix wave changes the UI after /test's QA stories ran, and nothing marks that evidence stale

**Summary:** `/review` Step 6.7 can auto-apply a fix wave that changes rendered UI after `/test`'s QA stories ran, and nothing re-runs those stories or marks the QA result as older than the wave.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:review` (code-mode Step 6.7, late findings routing) and the `/claude-tweaks:flow` step order

**Use case:**
A single-record `/flow` run in `auto` mode on a web UI record, `review-auto-apply-ceiling: medium`.

`/test` ran the record's QA stories (all passed). `/review` Step 6.5 (the design critique and audit) then returned nine low and medium findings. Under the ceiling, Step 6.7 auto-applied all of them as a fix wave of nine commits. Those commits changed rendered behaviour the stories describe: where two tooltips open, where focus and scroll land after paging, a new pending state on a control. One story's `verify` text had to be edited by the wave to stay true.

After the wave the pipeline re-verifies types, lint, tests and e2e (scoped per `test/verification.md`), but QA stories are not re-run, and nothing in the review summary, the verdict comment or the pipeline summary says the QA result predates the wave. "QA: all passed" then describes a UI ten commits old. In the observed run the controller noticed and re-ran the affected stories by hand.

Either of these would close it:

1. When Step 6.7 auto-applies a finding that touches a file listed in any story's `source_files`, mark those stories stale and re-run them after the wave, with the same tiering `/test` uses.
2. Have the review summary's QA line say so: "ran before the review's fix wave (N commits since); stories touching changed files: ...".

Related observation: the design pass is the last source of findings in `/review`, so on a UI record its fixes land after the most expensive verification (in the observed run a full verification had to be repeated). An option to run `design-wrapper review` before `/test`'s QA on records with a web surface would put those findings in front of QA instead of behind it.

Cost in the observed run: one extra full verification and a manual QA re-run.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0
