Surface: infra

**Related:** #2908, #2955, #2977, #3021, #3060

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3 dispatches read-only lens reviewers per `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`, as reproduction pairs or single reads. `review/SKILL.md:98` lists "Running verification or QA directly in review" as an anti-pattern, because mechanical checks belong in `/claude-tweaks:test`. The dispatch contract, however, never forbids a lens agent from running the project's suites, builds or servers:

- The per-lens Calibration + Output template (`:101-145`) carries no such rule. It is byte-pinned against `_shared/criteria-review-quality.md` by `tests/code-health-misc/criteria-fragments.test.js:70-96`, so it cannot be edited freely.
- The Foreground Execution Discipline note (`:58`) implicitly allows it. It speaks of "any lens, debate, refutation, or gap-sweep agent that runs a verification command (rather than only reading/reporting)".
- The post-fan-out sweep (`:146-158`) only diffs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` against the pre-dispatch listing. A stray dev server, mock server or test runner leaves no untracked file and is invisible to it.

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), a Fast-profile 3f Test Quality agent launched the project's full Playwright e2e suite in the background on the framework's default ports. This raced the ephemeral servers `/visual-review` starts for the same review. It produced wrong-harness failures (dev-build auth-gate failures the project documents as expected on `next dev`) and ended with "stopped with background work of its own still running" / "e2e: in-flight".

## Deliverables

1. Add an explicit rule to Step 3's dispatch prompt rules, outside the byte-identical Calibration block, alongside the Working Directory and Foreground Execution notes. The rule: lens, debate, refutation and gap-sweep agents never run the project's test suites, builds, dev servers or e2e runners. They read and report only, and mechanical verification belongs to `/claude-tweaks:test`. The rule must be part of what actually reaches each agent's prompt (the composed review-dispatch bundle), not just a maintainer-side note.
2. Reconcile the Foreground Execution Discipline note (`:58`) with the new rule, so it no longer implies running verification commands is an expected lens activity.
3. Extend the post-fan-out sweep with a report-only check for processes the fan-out left running: listeners that appeared on local TCP ports since the pre-dispatch snapshot, taken next to the existing `pre-dispatch-status.txt`. Report any new listener in the review summary's `Fan-out leftovers` section and log a `STAGED` line, mirroring the untracked-file handling. Never kill anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A conformance test asserts that the composed review-dispatch bundle (the text dispatched agents receive) contains the no-suites/builds/servers rule. Prove it goes red against the current text.
- `tests/code-health-misc/criteria-fragments.test.js` passes unchanged, since the Calibration block is untouched.
- `tests/review-dispatch-composition.test.js` passes, with the composed bundle still under `CEILING_BYTES` and no new `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS` entry.
- The sweep section documents the port-listener snapshot and diff, its report-only posture, and its `Fan-out leftovers`/`decisions.md` outputs. The conformance test pins this.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Code review's parallel reviewers are now told never to run your test suites or start servers, and the review reports any server they leave running.

## Technical Approach

Put the prohibition next to the existing discipline notes, in the source the composed review-dispatch bundle draws from, so it reaches agents with no per-tier duplication. For the listener check, capture a pre-dispatch snapshot (for example `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` on macOS/Linux, with a documented skip-and-log when the command is unavailable) into `{ctx-dir}`, then diff after the fan-out. Report by port and command name only.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — dispatch prompt rule, Foreground note reconciliation (`:58`), sweep extension (`:146-158`)
- `plugin/skills/review/review-summary-template.md` — `Fan-out leftovers` section lists leftover listeners
- `tests/review-lens-no-suites-conformance.test.js` — new conformance test for the composed-bundle rule and the sweep text

## Gotchas

- The Calibration + Output template is byte-identical with `_shared/criteria-review-quality.md` and pinned by a test. Do not put the new rule inside it.
- The composed review-dispatch bundle has a hard byte ceiling (`tests/review-dispatch-composition.test.js:71-78`). Measure headroom with `wc -c` before adding text, and keep the rule to one sentence.
- A listener diff can pick up unrelated processes another session started during the fan-out. Like the untracked-file sweep, it is report-only and must say it cannot attribute ownership. Never treat it as proof a lens agent misbehaved, and never kill anything.
- Refutation agents in Step 3.6 may legitimately need to read a test file. The rule forbids running suites, builds and servers, not reading code.

## Original request

review/step3-lens-dispatch.md: lens agents are never told not to run the project's test suites — one ran the full Playwright e2e suite in the background during the fan-out

**Summary:** A reproduction-pair lens agent (3f Test Quality, Fast profile) launched the project's full Playwright e2e run in the background on the framework's default ports during /review Step 3's fan-out, although its prompt said read-only review and foreground-only; the dispatch contract and the byte-identical Calibration + Output template never say "do not run the project's test suites or start servers".

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** review/step3-lens-dispatch.md (the per-lens dispatch prompt rules and the post-fan-out untracked-file sweep)

**Use case:** Step 3's lenses are read-only reviewers; mechanical verification belongs to /test (review/SKILL.md's own anti-pattern "Running verification or QA directly in review"). When a lens agent runs the suite anyway it (a) starts the project's dev server and mock on the default ports, racing the ephemeral servers /visual-review starts for the same review and any other session's server, (b) reports suite failures that are artefacts of the wrong harness (here: the dev-build auth-gate failures the project documents as structurally expected on `next dev`), and (c) violates the Foreground Execution Discipline — the harness note read "stopped with background work of its own still running" and the agent's reply said "e2e: in-flight". Nothing in the dispatch contract forbids it explicitly, and the post-fan-out sweep only diffs `git status` for untracked files, so a stray server or test runner is invisible to it. Expected: an explicit "never run the project's test suites, builds or servers — report only" line in the dispatch prompt rules (outside the byte-identical Calibration block), and a post-fan-out check for listeners on the framework's default ports (or spawned node processes) alongside the untracked-file sweep.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3002

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the verification pass stamp for any passing full run regardless of tree state (the write gate "never consults dirty", verify.js ~line 547), and `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true` only when the stored stamp was recorded against a clean tree at the current HEAD (`stampCoversCleanHead`, verify.js ~line 125). The dirty value comes from `gitInfo()` in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js`.

When a check regenerates a tracked file — the reported case is a Next.js production build rewriting `next-env.d.ts` — the tree is dirty at stamp time even though every check passed on the exact HEAD commit. `--stamp-status` then reads `verifiedHead: false`, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 re-triggers `/claude-tweaks:test`, and the re-run dirties the tree again. The only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out, or a manual restore-and-restamp.

A second, smaller gap from the same report: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` gives no guidance for a `--cmd` that needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path; the reporter needed two failed runs to learn that a committed wrapper script must put the working directory first on the import path.

## Deliverables

1. `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` accepts a `generated` list of path globs. `verify.js`'s dirty computation for the pass stamp ignores changes to paths matching those globs; any other dirty path still disqualifies the stamp exactly as today.
2. The stamp records which declared-generated paths were dirty at stamp time, so the exemption is auditable.
3. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the `generated` key (when to use it, and that it must name only files the checks regenerate) and adds a short note on `--cmd` wrappers needing environment variables or a working-directory-first import path.
4. `/claude-tweaks:init`'s verify-scope starter (`plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js`) accepts the new key without breaking existing scope files.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full passing run whose only dirty path matches a declared `generated` glob produces a stamp for which `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true`, and the stamp lists that path.
2. A full passing run with any other dirty path still produces `verifiedHead: false`.
3. A scope file without `generated` behaves exactly as today.
4. `node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` and the verify CLI tests pass, with new cases for 1–3.

## Release Note

Verification can now earn a passing stamp when a check regenerates a declared generated file, instead of forcing a second run.

## Technical Approach

Extend the verify-scope declaration parser to read `generated`, pass the globs into the dirty computation used for the pass stamp (not the general report's `dirty`, which other readers may rely on), and record the exempted paths in the stamp. Option (b) from the original request — exempting any path that was clean before the run and dirtied by it — is rejected: a check that rewrites source (a formatter or `lint --fix`) would then vouch for a tree that differs from HEAD. Explicit declaration keeps that case disqualifying.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — stamp write and `--stamp-status` dirty handling
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — `gitInfo()` dirty computation; add a filtered variant for the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` — record exempted generated paths in the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — parse `generated` from `verify-scope.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js` — starter scope file compatibility
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — document `generated` and the `--cmd` wrapper note
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- #2806 (untangling `verify/args.js`'s parseArgs, PR #2836) is in flight in the same module family; land after it merges or rebase onto it to avoid conflicts.
- #3002 (per-suite stamps for chunked runs) changes the same stamp format; coordinate the stamp schema so both additions compose.
- The stamp's existing semantics (#1921: the runner is the only writer; #1784: no agent-side writes) must not change.

## Original request

bin/verify.js pass stamp: reads dirty when a check regenerates a tracked file

**Component:** `bin/verify.js` pass stamp (`--stamp-status`, `verifiedHead`) and `test/verification.md` "Verification pass stamp", plugin version 6.134.1.

**Kind:** Gap.

**What happened.** A project's full check list includes a production build of a Next.js app. That build rewrites a tracked, generated type-declaration file (`next-env.d.ts`) in place, so the working tree is dirty at the moment `verify.js` writes its pass stamp. Every check passed on the exact HEAD commit, but `--stamp-status` then reports `verifiedHead: false`, and `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 treats `TEST_PASSED=true` plus a non-verifying stamp as "re-trigger `/claude-tweaks:test`". Re-running the same full set dirties the tree again, so the only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out.

**Why it matters.** The stamp's dirty rule exists to stop a pass on uncommitted source from vouching for a commit. A file the checks themselves regenerate is a different case, and today it forces a redundant run (minutes of wall-clock per review) or a manual restore-and-rerun on every project whose build touches a tracked generated file.

**Suggested behaviour.** One of: (a) let `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` declare `generated` paths the stamp's dirty check ignores; (b) have `verify.js` compare the dirty set before and after the run and treat paths that were clean before the run and dirtied only by the checks as non-disqualifying, recording them in the stamp; or (c) document the workaround in `test/verification.md` (restore the generated file, then re-stamp with a check set that does not regenerate it).

**Second, related observation from the same run.** A project with no `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and a Python test list that needs environment variables has no documented way to express `--cmd tests=` other than a hand-written wrapper script, and a script-driven test runner resolves the project's packages differently from `python -m pytest` (the script's directory, not the working directory, is first on the import path). A short note in `test/verification.md` — "when `--cmd` needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path, commit a wrapper in the project and put the working directory first on the import path" — would have saved two failed verification runs.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Under `integration-model: pr-first`, every phase that commits ends with a phase-exit push (`plugin/skills/_shared/git-discipline.md`, "Phase-exit push" section, line 36). That section pushes and handles push failure (warn and continue), but never reads the PR's merge state.

When the integration branch moves during a long build and the run's draft PR starts to conflict, GitHub runs no `pull_request` workflows for the conflicting PR. The PR shows no CI jobs at all, which reads exactly like "CI pending". In the reported run (plugin 6.134.1), the conflict (`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`) was found only because the orchestrator happened to query the PR. Pipeline Step 2.5's divergence check runs once at start, and multi-spec re-checks only at the finish step, so a conflict that appears mid-run goes unnoticed until the merge decision.

The repo already reads PR merge state elsewhere: `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`'s `resolvePrStateByNumber` returns `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus` (#2367), and `_shared/github-pr-scan.md` flags `DIRTY` pending-review PRs. The catch-up procedure exists too ("Catching a branch up with `main`", same file).

## Deliverables

1. After each successful phase-exit push, when `run-state.json` carries a `pr` object, read the PR's merge state via `resolvePrStateByNumber`, best-effort and fail-open.
2. When it reports `DIRTY`, state it in the phase output and log an `AUTO` decision-log entry naming the PR and phase.
3. In `auto` mode, run "Catching a branch up with `main`" (fetch, merge in the worktree, resolve per the merge-conflict procedure, re-push) before the next phase starts. In `interactive`/`hybrid`, surface the conflict and the catch-up command; do not add a new mid-flow stop.
4. A merge-state read failure, or a state of `UNKNOWN`, logs nothing alarming and changes nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A phase exit on a run whose PR reports `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY` prints a conflict line and writes one `AUTO` entry to `decisions.md`.
2. In `auto` mode the next phase starts on a branch that has been caught up with the integration branch, and the re-push triggers the PR's `pull_request` workflows.
3. A run with no `pr` in `run-state.json`, a `local-merge` run, and a `current-branch` run behave exactly as today.
4. A failed or `UNKNOWN` merge-state read never stops or slows a phase beyond the one read.

## Release Note

Pipeline runs now notice when their draft PR starts conflicting with the base branch, instead of finding out at merge time.

## Technical Approach

Add a short "Post-push merge-state check" paragraph to the Phase-exit push section that calls a small CLI (or an existing `hooks.js` subcommand) wrapping `resolvePrStateByNumber`, so the check is mechanical rather than an agent-composed `gh` call. Reuse the existing catch-up procedure for the auto-mode remedy; do not add a second merge procedure.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/git-discipline.md` — Phase-exit push section gains the merge-state check and its auto-mode remedy
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — cross-reference from the PR lifecycle
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js` — `resolvePrStateByNumber`, reused
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — if the check is exposed as a subcommand
- `docs/hooks.md` — document any new subcommand

## Gotchas

- GitHub computes mergeability asynchronously; immediately after a push `mergeable` is often `UNKNOWN`. Treat `UNKNOWN` as no signal (optionally one short delayed re-read), never as a conflict.
- Auto catch-up merges into the run's branch mid-pipeline; it must use the worktree-scoped push form (`git -C {worktree} push origin {branch}`) and must not run when the worktree has uncommitted changes.
- The phase-exit push's failure posture is "degrade per attempt, never persist" — the new check must follow it.

## Original request

_shared/git-discipline.md phase-exit push: does not notice a conflicting PR

**Component:** `_shared/git-discipline.md` "Phase-exit push" / `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` (pr-first integration model), plugin version 6.134.1.

**Kind:** Gap (the skill has no opinion where it should).

**What happened.** In a single-record `/flow` run under `integration-model: pr-first`, the build phase's exit push landed on a draft PR whose base branch had moved during the build and now conflicted in two files. The forge runs no `pull_request` workflow for a PR in a conflicting state, so the PR showed no CI jobs at all. Nothing in the phase-exit procedure reads the PR's merge state, so the run carried on to the test step with CI silently absent; the conflict was found only because the orchestrator happened to query the PR's checks and then its `mergeStateStatus`.

**Why it matters.** The pipeline's Step 2.5 divergence check is a point-in-time check at pipeline start, and the multi-spec flow re-checks only at the final finish step. A long build (hours) has a real window for the base to move. A conflicting PR costs a merge plus a full re-verification, and that is cheapest to learn at the first phase exit, not at the merge decision. A missing CI run also reads exactly like "CI pending".

**Suggested behaviour.** After each phase-exit push, when `run-state.json` carries a `pr` object: read the PR's merge state (`gh pr view {n} --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus`, best-effort, fail-open). When it reports a conflict, say so in the phase output and log an `AUTO` decision; in `auto` mode, run the existing catch-up (fetch the integration branch, merge in the worktree, resolve per the merge-conflict procedure) before the next phase instead of after the last one. A forge that reports a stale conflicting state can be told apart by attempting the merge locally.

**Evidence shape (scrubbed).** Push at commit A: PR checks list only push-triggered workflows. `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`. After merging the base and pushing commit B: all `pull_request` jobs run.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2389, #2908, #2954, #2955, #3035

## Current State

The report, filed via `/claude-tweaks:feedback` against plugin 6.129.0 from a private-project run on 2026-10-04, describes a double path. `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6.7 staged a Design-Quality audit `warning` as `staged/review-design-1.patch`, and `design-wrapper polish` Step 5 then dispatched the same finding's `suggestion` (`harden`), applying the identical `aria-label` edit. The staged patch went stale and had to be removed by hand.

On the current tree this hand-off already exists. It shipped in PR #2389 (merged 2026-09-23, first released in v6.130.0, one release after the reporter's 6.129.0 build), which fixed records #2280 and #2281:

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:342` (Step 6.7 item 3, "Write the disposition back to the audit cache") sets `dispositionByReview: {status, at}` on the matching audit-cache entry by `id`. The routing outcome maps to a status, and STAGED becomes `staged`.
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md:66-72` checks `dispositionByReview` first. Any `source: "audit"` entry carrying it is "Skipped entirely" by Step 5's suggestion-driven dispatch. The rationale is at `:78-87`.
- `tests/review-polish-disposition-conformance.test.js` pins both halves: the write-back with all five statuses, and polish's check-order ahead of `suggestion`.

The reported scenario (a staged audit finding later re-applied by polish's `harden` dispatch) is therefore the exact case #2389 closes. The reporter's run used a build that predates it. What remains is confirming that and closing the record.

## Deliverables

1. Confirm on the current integration branch that the reported scenario is covered. A `source: "audit"` Design-Quality finding with `suggestion: "harden"`, routed STAGED by Step 6.7 under `review-auto-apply-ceiling: low`, gets `dispositionByReview.status: "staged"` and is skipped by polish Step 5. Check this against the two prose sites and the conformance test listed above.
2. If the conformance test does not already assert the specific STAGED-then-skipped pairing, add one assertion that does. The existing test covers the field and the check order generically. Otherwise make no code change.
3. Close this record with a comment naming PR #2389 / v6.130.0 as the fix, so the reporter knows to upgrade.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/review-polish-disposition-conformance.test.js` passes on the current branch, and it, or one added assertion, covers a STAGED disposition causing polish Step 5 to skip the entry.
- No change to `code-mode-steps.md` or `polish.md` prose unless the verification finds an actual gap. Any such gap is described in the closing comment.
- `npm test` passes in full.
- The record is closed with a comment citing #2389 and v6.130.0.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: confirmed the review and polish double-apply of a staged design finding was already fixed in 6.130.0.

## Technical Approach

This is a read-and-confirm pass. Read Step 6.7 item 3 and polish's four-way consumption table, then run the existing conformance suite. Only if the STAGED pairing is not pinned, add a single assertion to that suite in its existing style.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 item 3 disposition write-back (verify only)
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` — four-way consumption table, `dispositionByReview`-first check (verify only)
- `tests/review-polish-disposition-conformance.test.js` — confirm, or add, the STAGED-then-skipped assertion

## Gotchas

- The reporter's "Expected" offered two fixes: defer in Step 6.7, or have polish mark the patch superseded. #2389 implemented a third shape: review writes its disposition and polish skips it. That satisfies the report's stated outcome, one owner per audit finding. Do not add either of the reporter's mechanisms on top, since that would create a second hand-off for the same case.
- Standalone `/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper polish` (no `/review` Step 6.7 in the run) deliberately keeps the old behavior (`polish.md:86-87`). That is not a regression.

## Original request

review Step 6.7 + design-wrapper polish Step 5: an audit finding is staged as a patch and then applied again by polish's suggestion dispatch

**Summary:** With `polish` still in the run's step list, `/review` Step 6.7 stages a Design-Quality audit `warning` as a patch under the `review-auto-apply-ceiling: low` routing, and `design-wrapper polish` Step 5 then dispatches that same finding's own `suggestion` command (`harden`), which applies the identical edit — the staged patch goes stale and must be removed by hand or reaches the Review Console already applied.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 (late findings routing) and `skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` Step 5 (suggestion-driven dispatch)

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow` on a frontend record with the default step list (review then polish), `review-auto-apply-ceiling: low`, `design-critique: auto`.
2. Let `design-wrapper review` produce one audit finding of severity P2/`warning` whose `suggestion` names `harden` (e.g. a missing `aria-label` on an element).
3. Observe `/review` Step 6.7 stage it as `staged/review-design-1.patch` (validated with `git apply --check` at staging time) with a ledger back-reference.
4. Let the polish phase run: Step 5 reads the same audit cache entry and dispatches `harden`, which applies the same edit in the working tree.
5. Run polish's re-verify / reach the Review Console: the staged patch no longer passes `git apply --check`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: one owner per audit finding — either Step 6.7 defers a finding that polish's suggestion-driven dispatch will take (when `polish` is still in the step list and the suggestion names a non-manual command), logging `deferred to polish (suggestion: {command})`, or polish's Step 5 marks the matching staged patch superseded (rename to `.applied` or delete, with a decisions.md line) when its dispatch lands.
Actual: both consumers read the same audit cache entry with no hand-off between them. In one run in a private project (plugin 6.129.0, 2026-10-04), the review phase staged the patch at 16:21 and the polish phase's `harden` applied the identical `aria-label` edit at 18:35; the operator removed the patch by hand and logged it as superseded. Had it survived to the console, it would have failed the apply check and triggered the slower Invariant re-derivation for an edit already in the tree. Why-chain: `design-wrapper review` writes the cache and `/review` stages in the same pass with no "polish will take this" marker; the two consumers were added by different records. Observed cost: one hand cleanup, no lost work; the double path holds in any project.

**Definition:** Clear — the cheaper fix (defer in Step 6.7 when `polish` remains in the step list) closes the double path; the alternative (polish marks the patch superseded) is a fallback, not an undecided choice.

**Plugin version:** 6.129.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2907, #2908, #2954, #3049

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3 runs reproduction pairs. Two agents run the same lens, and `bin/review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction` pairs their findings via `categoriseReproduction` (`plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js:285`). A pair is a candidate only when `sameLocation(fa, fb, LINE_TOLERANCE_REPRODUCTION)` holds (`:300`): path exact, `Math.abs(line delta) <= 2` (`:191-198`, constant `:8`). After that comes the #1980 substance check (`sameSubstance`, Jaccard ≥ `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4`, `:26`, `:248-252`). The same ±2 rule is restated in prose at `plugin/skills/_shared/multi-agent-coordination.md:49` and `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md:90-93`, and pinned by `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js:321`.

The rule fails on a finding inside one multi-line statement. In the reported run, both agents of the error-handling pair flagged the same issue, a value read inside a multi-line call argument after an external side effect. They anchored it on two different lines of that statement, 3 lines apart. `sameLocation` rejected the pair before substance was ever compared. The result was 0 confirmed and 2 unconfirmed, the real finding was routed to the Review Console's Low-confidence section instead of Step 3 Routing, and the reviewer had to confirm it by hand with the direct-verification override. Reported via `/claude-tweaks:feedback` against plugin 6.133.0.

## Deliverables

1. Add a substance-gated wider tolerance to reproduction pairing. A same-path pair whose line delta is above `LINE_TOLERANCE_REPRODUCTION` (2) but within a new, wider bound (for example 5, matching `LINE_TOLERANCE_DEBATE`) is a candidate only when its `substanceSimilarity` clears a stricter floor than `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN`. Today's ±2 path is unchanged, including the `null`-substance-pairs-as-match rule. An unknown (`null`) substance never qualifies for the wider band.
2. Export the new bound and the stricter floor as named constants next to the existing ones (`:8-26`, export block `:443-448`).
3. Update the prose twins (`_shared/multi-agent-coordination.md:49` and `review/step3-lens-dispatch.md:90-93`) to state the two-tier rule, so the prose and the code agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test in `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js` passes two findings on the same path, 3 lines apart, with near-identical text and the same severity bucket. It asserts one confirmed and zero unconfirmed. Prove it goes red against the current ±2-only rule.
- A test with the same 3-line delta but substantively different text (below the stricter floor) asserts both stay unconfirmed.
- A test with a 3-line delta and one side missing its text (`null` substance) asserts both stay unconfirmed.
- The existing ±2, #1980 near-location, and #733 severity-contested tests pass unchanged.
- `tests/bin-lib/review-coordination/cli.test.js` passes unchanged.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Review's reproduction pairs now confirm a finding both agents reported a few lines apart within the same statement, instead of leaving it unconfirmed.

## Technical Approach

In `categoriseReproduction`'s candidate gather (`:297-302`), accept a B finding when `sameLocation(fa, fb, LINE_TOLERANCE_REPRODUCTION)` holds, or when `sameLocation(fa, fb, <wider bound>)` holds and `substanceSimilarity(fa, fb) >= <strict floor>`. Everything downstream (eligible filter, best-score selection, `reconcileSeverity`) stays unchanged. Keep `findingsMatch`'s default untouched unless a caller needs the same widening, and check its callers first.

The reporter's other option, anchoring both findings to the enclosing statement's line range, is not chosen. `coordination.js` is pure and receives only `path:line` plus text, so finding a statement range would mean reading and parsing source files inside a module that does no I/O today.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` — `categoriseReproduction`: substance-gated wider tolerance band; new exported constants
- `plugin/skills/_shared/multi-agent-coordination.md` — restate the two-tier line rule (`:49`)
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — restate the two-tier line rule (`:90-93`)
- `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js` — 3-line-apart confirm, different-substance, and null-substance cases

## Gotchas

- Choose the stricter floor with a fixture, not by intuition. Jaccard over tokenized finding text is sensitive to normalization, so check the reported pair's actual text scores above it and an unrelated same-statement pair scores below it.
- The wider band must not change the #1980 `nearLocation` behavior for pairs within ±2. That branch fires only when every same-location candidate is substantively different. Make sure a wide-band candidate that fails the strict floor is simply not a candidate, rather than being reported as `nearLocation`.
- `detectCrossLensOverlap` already uses `LINE_TOLERANCE_DEBATE` (5) for a different purpose (`:368`). If the new bound reuses that value, give it its own constant name so the two can diverge later.

## Original request

review-coordination categorise-reproduction: one finding inside a multi-line statement splits into two unconfirmed findings

**Summary:** Both agents of a reproduction pair reported the same finding inside one multi-line statement, 3 lines apart, so the ±2 line match left a real finding unconfirmed.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** claude-tweaks review, Step 3 reproduction pairs (`bin/review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction`, `categoriseReproduction` in `bin/lib/coordination.js`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Run a medium-tier `/claude-tweaks:review` on a diff where a value is read inside a multi-line call argument, after an external side effect.
2. Both agents of the error-handling pair flag it. Agent A anchors the finding on one line of the statement and agent B on another line, 3 lines away.
3. Run `categorise-reproduction` on the two findings files.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: findings that agree in substance and sit inside the same multi-line statement reproduce. One fix would widen the line tolerance when the same-substance score is high; another would anchor both reports to the enclosing statement's line range before comparing.
Actual: the rule is "path exact, line ±2", so the result was 0 confirmed and 2 unconfirmed. The real finding would have gone to the Review Console's Low-confidence section instead of Step 3 Routing. The reviewer had to confirm it by hand with the direct-verification override.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.133.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3132

## Current State

`gitCommittedToRemoval(real, root)` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js:116-121`) gates the win32 long-path fallback in `attemptLongPathRemoval` (`:133`). It runs `git worktree list --porcelain` and finds the target's entry with `(safeReal(wt.path) || wt.path) === real` (`:119`). It returns `!entry || entry.prunable`. In other words, "no matching entry" reads as "git committed to removal", which permits a force-delete.

`safeReal` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-detect.js:18-20`) swallows every `realpathSync` error and returns `null`. When resolution fails for a registered entry, the comparison falls back to the raw porcelain path against the already-resolved `real`. On any path that differs from its realpath (a symlinked ancestor, macOS `/private` prefixes) that comparison misses. A still-registered, healthy worktree then reads as absent, and the gate opens. The header comment (`:115`) says "An unreadable list fails closed", but this per-entry branch is fail-open.

Reaching it requires `realpath` to fail with something other than ENOENT on an intact, registered worktree directory that resolved moments earlier in the same pass, for example an ancestor permission change or a symlink loop. This is hardening, not a live bug. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3b, single agent, direct-verified, low).

## Deliverables

1. In `gitCommittedToRemoval`, a registered entry whose path fails to resolve with any error other than ENOENT makes the function return `false` (fail closed). Such an entry can never be silently treated as non-matching.
2. A registered entry whose path fails with ENOENT is treated as non-matching. A path that does not exist cannot be the existing target directory, so this keeps today's mid-deletion behavior.
3. `gitCommittedToRemoval` gains an injectable realpath seam, for example an optional third `{ realpath = fs.realpathSync }` argument, so a test can force a non-ENOENT failure on one entry. Existing callers keep the two-argument form.
4. The header comment above the function states the per-entry fail-closed rule alongside the existing "unreadable list fails closed" sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` injects a realpath that throws a non-ENOENT error (for example `EACCES`) for the target's registered entry, and asserts `gitCommittedToRemoval` returns `false`. Prove it goes red against the current `safeReal(wt.path) || wt.path` fallback.
- A unit test whose injected realpath throws ENOENT for a non-target entry still returns the same result as today for the target.
- The existing #2566 tests in that file (the mid-deletion finish case at `:606-617` and the dirty/locked refusal cases) pass unchanged.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

The worktree-reap long-path fallback now refuses to force-delete when a registered worktree's path cannot be resolved, instead of treating it as already removed.

## Technical Approach

Replace the `safeReal(wt.path) || wt.path` fallback with an explicit try/catch around the injected realpath. On ENOENT, the entry is non-matching. On any other error, short-circuit the whole function to `false`. Keep `safeReal` itself unchanged, because it is shared with `flow-preflight.js`, `hooks.js`, `context.js` and `pre-tool-use.js`, and those callers rely on its null-on-any-error contract.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — `gitCommittedToRemoval`: per-entry fail-closed resolution, injectable realpath, header comment
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` — non-ENOENT and ENOENT injection tests

## Gotchas

- Do not change `safeReal` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-detect.js`. Several other modules depend on it returning `null` for any failure. The fix belongs at this one call site.
- Fail closed means the function returns `false` as soon as any registered entry is unresolvable for a non-ENOENT reason, even if that entry might not be the target. An unresolvable entry cannot be proven not to be the target, and a false `false` only routes to the existing removal-failed escalation, which is the safe outcome.
- The mid-deletion test at `:606-617` is skipped on some platforms (`MID_DELETE_SKIP`). Check that the new injection tests do not depend on a real mid-deletion state, so they run everywhere.

## Original request

reconcile: gitCommittedToRemoval treats an unresolvable registered entry as absent (fail-open branch)

## Current State

`#2930` gated the win32 worktree-reap fallback in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` on `gitCommittedToRemoval(real, root)`: after a failed `git worktree remove`, the worktree is gone from `git worktree list` or marked `prunable`. Its per-entry match is `(safeReal(wt.path) || wt.path) === real` — when `realpath` fails for a registered entry, the raw porcelain path is compared against the resolved `real`, rarely matches, and the entry reads as absent, i.e. "git committed to removal". The header comment says the gate fails closed; this branch is fail-open. Reaching it needs `realpath` to fail on an intact, registered worktree directory that resolved moments earlier in the same pass (ancestor permission change, symlink loop), so it is hardening, not a live bug. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3b single agent, direct-verified, low).

## Deliverables

- [ ] An entry whose path cannot be resolved for any reason other than ENOENT makes `gitCommittedToRemoval` return false (fail closed); an ENOENT entry cannot be the existing target directory and is treated as non-matching

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test with an injected realpath failure (non-ENOENT) on the target's registered entry gets `false`
- [ ] The existing #2566 tests (mid-deletion finish, dirty/locked refusal) still pass

Surface: infra

## Current State

In an `integration-model: pr-first` run, after the materialize commit and before a PR is recorded, `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:1566`) denies every covered file-tool write with "no PR is recorded for this run". A 6.129.0 run hit this twice: first on a plan file, which is correct because the gate exists to block implementation writes before the PR, and second on the scratch PR-body file the agent composed in a **gitignored directory inside the worktree** before calling `gh pr create --body-file`. That second denial is a deadlock: the gate demands the PR while blocking the file needed to open it.

Checked against the tree:

- The PR-body path documented in `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md:315-325` is `/tmp/pr-early-body-{run-id}-{n}.md`. Since #1678 (v6.114.1), the stamps gate's file-tool branch already exempts a target that is provably not inside any git repo (`pre-tool-use.js:1636-1690`). So the documented `/tmp` path is not blocked on POSIX.
- A **gitignored path inside the worktree** has no such exemption in this gate. `isStampsGateExemptTarget` (`pre-tool-use.js`) exempts only `isPipelineBookkeeping` and `isPolicyFile` targets. The sibling worktree-required gate already exempts gitignored targets through `isUntrackedOrIgnored` (#1395, `pre-tool-use.js:278` and its call site near `:914`, which leaves a `gate-exempt-gitignored` breadcrumb). The two gates therefore disagree on the same path class. A gitignored file cannot land on the branch (no `git add -f` without an explicit commit, which the gate's own git-write branch still covers), so it cannot affect what the PR stamp protects.

## Deliverables

1. Extend `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`'s exemptions to cover a target that `isUntrackedOrIgnored(repoRoot, targetPath)` proves gitignored in its own repo. Reuse the existing helper, keep its fail-closed behavior (absolute path only; indeterminate or not-ignored stays denied), and leave the same `gate-exempt-gitignored` breadcrumb the worktree-required gate writes.
2. Add tests to `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js`:
   - with no PR recorded, a Write to a gitignored path inside the worktree is allowed, and a breadcrumb is written;
   - with no PR recorded, a Write to a tracked or not-ignored path is still denied;
   - a relative target path is still denied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a pr-first run with a materialize commit but no recorded PR, a `Write` to a gitignored file inside the run's worktree is allowed by `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`, and a `gate-exempt-gitignored` event is appended.
- In the same state, a `Write` to a tracked or not-ignored file in the worktree is still denied with the existing "no PR is recorded" message.
- The new cases in `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js` cover both outcomes plus the relative-path fail-closed case.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Fixed the pre-PR bookkeeping guard blocking writes to gitignored scratch files, which could stop an agent from writing the draft PR body.

## Technical Approach

Add the `isUntrackedOrIgnored` check to `isStampsGateExemptTarget`, or alongside its call site at the end of the file-tool branch, so it runs after the foreign-target scoping and before the stamp checks. The helper already handles absolute-path-only and git-error fail-closed cases. Match the breadcrumb shape the worktree-required gate uses so `/tidy` or an operator can audit both gates' gitignored allows the same way.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — `isStampsGateExemptTarget` / `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`: add the gitignored-target exemption with a breadcrumb
- `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js` — gitignored-allow, tracked-deny and relative-deny cases

## Gotchas

- This repo has a project skill for exactly this kind of change, `pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions`. Follow its discipline for adding a scoping exemption to these deny gates.
- Keep the exemption limited to file-tool writes and gitignored targets. Do not widen it to "untracked" in general: `isUntrackedOrIgnored`'s own header (#1395) explains why untracked-but-not-ignored stays gated.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the 6.129.0 incident's PR-body file sat in a gitignored worktree directory rather than at the documented `/tmp` path, and nothing else (for example Windows resolving `/tmp` inside the repo) caused that denial. `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md:316-317` already notes that `Write` and `Bash` can resolve `/tmp` differently on Windows. Check this against the gate's foreign-target branch on a Windows path before closing.

## Original request

Bookkeeping-stamps gate blocks the Write of the PR body file needed to open the PR it demands

## Observation

In an `integration-model: pr-first` run, after the materialize commit lands and before a PR is recorded, `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` (`bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) denies every covered `Write`, with "no PR is recorded for this run — build/worktree-setup.md Step 6 … is non-skippable". That includes the `Write` of the PR body file that `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 3 tells the agent to compose before `gh pr create --body-file <file>`.

So the gate demands the draft PR while blocking the file needed to open it. Observed in plugin 6.129.0 with two denied writes: a plan file, then the scratch PR-body file in a gitignored worktree directory. The run only got unblocked by piping the body through `gh pr create --body-file -` (stdin heredoc) and then `hooks.js record-pr`.

Cost: two denied writes and one re-composition of the PR body. An agent that doesn't think of stdin may instead log the "FAILED" degrade line and continue PR-less.

## Suggested change

Either of these:

1. Exempt paths that cannot affect the branch the stamp protects: gitignored scratch dirs, `/tmp`, the run dir.
2. Have `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 3 compose the body via stdin (`gh pr create --body-file -`) by default, so the documented procedure never needs a covered write before the PR exists.

_Filed from a wrap-up Review Console (upstream feedback row), approved by the repo owner._

Surface: infra

## Current State

`ledgerProbe` in `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js:366-418` reads `{run-dir}/ledger.md` first. When that file is absent, it falls back to every `*-ledger.md` under `{worktree}/docs/plans/` (`:378-379`) and picks among them with two heuristics:

- **Exactly one candidate**: the probe treats it as "unambiguously this run's" (`:380-388`), without checking.
- **Two or more candidates, none naming one of this run's records at a `-{n}-`/`-{n}.` boundary** (`namesRecord`, `:362-364`): the probe counts **every** candidate (`:396`), deliberately failing toward over-counting (#2563).

Both heuristics assume the only ledgers in `docs/plans/` are this run's own. That is false in this repo. Finished runs' ledgers stay committed on `main` (for example `docs/plans/2026-10-03-record-2853-ledger.md` and `docs/plans/2026-10-04-record-2772-ledger.md` are tracked today), so every new worktree branched from `main` inherits them. A run that never created its own docs/plans ledger therefore gets either a stranger's ledger counted as its own (one candidate) or all the strangers' ledgers summed (several candidates). This is what happened on #2852's wrap-up: `pack.ledger` reported an unrelated, still-active run's ledger.

## Deliverables

1. Attribute ledgers to the run by ownership, not by filename heuristics. Treat a `docs/plans/*-ledger.md` as this run's only when this run's branch added or modified it relative to its merge base. Keep `namesRecord` only as a secondary tie-break among owned candidates.
2. When no candidate is owned by this run, report zero items. Also expose the unattributed candidates in a distinct field (for example `unattributedFiles`) so a human can still see them. Never sum them into `open` or `total`.
3. Update `pack.test.js` with cases for: one inherited (unowned) ledger, several inherited ledgers with none owned, one owned ledger alongside inherited ones, and the `{run-dir}/ledger.md` precedence (unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose `docs/plans/` holds only ledgers inherited from the merge base gets `pack.ledger` with `open: 0`, `total: 0`, and those files listed under the unattributed field, not under `files`.
- A worktree with one ledger added on its branch plus inherited ledgers counts only the added ledger's items.
- `{run-dir}/ledger.md`, when present, still takes precedence with unchanged output.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Fixed wrap-up counting open items from other runs' ledger files as if they belonged to the current run.

## Technical Approach

The probe already runs where a base ref is available: wrap-up's pack has the run's integration branch and merge base for its other probes. Derive owned files with `git diff --name-only {merge-base}...HEAD -- docs/plans/` through the probe's injectable `deps` seam, so the tests stay hermetic. Keep the existing #2563 rationale in mind. The over-count fallback existed because the only alternative was silently hiding the run's own items, and ownership-by-diff removes that dilemma. Update the comment block at `:380-396` to match.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `ledgerProbe` (366-418): ownership-based attribution plus an unattributed field
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — inherited/owned ledger cases
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md` — read-only check: its Location section's "one ledger per pipeline run" wording should still hold after the change

## Gotchas

- A run whose ledger was created and committed earlier on the same branch still counts as owned, because the merge-base diff includes it. A ledger that only exists uncommitted in the worktree also needs handling. Include untracked or modified files from `git status --porcelain -- docs/plans/` along with the diff.
- Any consumer that reads `pack.ledger.files` (wrap-up's resolve gate, the Review Console) must not start treating the new unattributed field as blocking. Grep for `ledger.files` and `pack.ledger` consumers before changing the shape.
- The accumulation of finished runs' ledgers on `main` is itself a separate cleanup question. It is out of scope here, and the probe must be correct regardless.

## Original request

wrap-up-pack.js's ledger probe can match an unrelated run's ledger file

Origin: wrap-up (#2852)
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

**Related:** none

Context: wrap-up's ledger probe (bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js) falls back to a bare docs/plans/*-ledger.md glob when a run has no run-dir ledger.md. On #2852's wrap-up it matched an unrelated, still-active run's shared ledger instead of reporting none.

Scope: Scope the fallback to this run's own feature-slug, or verify the match actually belongs to this run, before reporting it as pack.ledger.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3044 (item 1 of the original request — the AC-forwarding sample's sanctioned writer — is already its own `ready` record; out of scope here)

## Current State

The original report bundles four friction points from one `/flow` run on 6.132.0 (Windows, worktree-isolated). Checked against this tree:

1. **AC-forwarding sample path unwritable from a worktree session** — already shaped as #3044, which covers exactly this. Excluded from this record.
2. **`computeDiffFacts` input shape vs its documented call — confirmed.** `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md:19` says to compute diff facts "via `bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js`'s `computeDiffFacts` over the branch's `git diff --numstat` output". `plugin/skills/wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md:30` uses the same phrasing. But `computeDiffFacts(files)` (`plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js:25-29`) takes the parsed `[{path, additions, deletions}]` array, which `parseNumstat` produces. `parseNumstat` is exported from `plugin/bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js:40,145`. Neither doc names the parser, so following the prose literally passes a raw string and throws.
3. **Circular-dependency warnings on the documented security-hardening invocation — confirmed, but the false-clean claim is not reproduced.** Running `plugin/skills/review/focus-criterion-passes.md:12`'s direct `require` of `candidates-security-hardening.js` emits `Accessing non-existent property 'listTrackedSourceFiles' … inside circular dependency`, along with the same warning for `isGlobDiscoveredTestFile`, `extractModuleExports`, `escapeRegExp` and `listTrackedFiles`. The cause is require order. `candidates-security-hardening.js:143-144` requires `./candidates-dead-code` before `./focus-generators`. `candidates-experiment-cleanup.js:60-61` does the same and also emits warnings when required directly. The ordering rule documented at `candidates-abstraction-police.js:56-68` says to require the registry first, because otherwise Node hands a sibling generator a partially loaded `candidates-dead-code` exports object and its helpers bind to `undefined`. On this repo, `scanSecurityHardening(process.cwd())` still returns a non-empty `{candidates: [...]}`. The scan itself therefore works here, and the generator actually affected by the half-loaded exports is `candidates-abstraction-police.js` in that same process.
4. **`log-decision.js --reversibility` rejects the documented qualifier form — confirmed.** `plugin/bin/log-decision.js:51` accepts only `high|med|low|n/a`. Meanwhile `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md:154,307,333` mandates log lines such as `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).`, and `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js:51` renders `Reversibility: ${reversibility}.`. The sanctioned writer cannot produce the documented line.

## Deliverables

1. **Item 2:** in `build/dispatch.md:19` and `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md:30`, state that the numstat output is parsed with `parseNumstat` (`bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js`) before `computeDiffFacts` is called. Give a one-line runnable `node -e` composing the two.
2. **Item 3:** fix the require order in `candidates-security-hardening.js` and `candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` so `./focus-generators` is required before `./candidates-dead-code`, matching `candidates-abstraction-police.js`'s documented rule. Add a regression test: requiring each `candidates-*.js` module directly in a fresh `node` process emits no `inside circular dependency` warning.
3. **Item 4:** make `log-decision.js --reversibility` accept a tier with a trailing parenthetical qualifier (`high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)`). Validate the tier against the existing enum and render the qualifier verbatim, so the written line matches `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s mandated form. A bare tier keeps working unchanged. Check that `claim-log.js`'s `ACTION_RE` (`plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js:23`) still parses lines that carry a qualifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `build/dispatch.md` and `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md` name `parseNumstat` as the step between `git diff --numstat` and `computeDiffFacts`.
- `node -e "require('./plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js')" 2>&1 | grep -c "circular dependency"` prints `0`, and the same holds for every other `candidates-*.js` module. A test pins this.
- `log-decision.js --reversibility "high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)"` exits 0 and writes `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).`. `--reversibility "bogus (x)"` still exits non-zero. Tests cover both cases.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Fixed misleading circular-dependency warnings from code-health scanners and let the decision logger record reversibility notes the pipeline docs require.

## Technical Approach

The three items are independent, small, and touch disjoint files, so build them as three separate commits. Item 3: swap the two require lines in each offending module. The warning test spawns `node -e "require(...)"` per module and asserts that stderr contains no `circular dependency` string. Item 4: parse `^(high|med|low|n/a)(\s+\(.+\))?$`, validate group 1 against `REVERSIBILITY`, and pass the full string through to `formatEntry`. Item 2 is prose only.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` — name `parseNumstat` before `computeDiffFacts` (line 19)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md` — same correction (line 30)
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js` — require `./focus-generators` before `./candidates-dead-code`
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` — same require-order fix
- `plugin/bin/log-decision.js` — accept a tier with a trailing parenthetical qualifier
- `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js` — render the qualifier verbatim
- `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js` — confirm `ACTION_RE` tolerates a qualifier
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.test.js` — add the no-circular-warning assertion (or a sibling test covering every `candidates-*.js`)

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the reporter's `[]` result from `scanSecurityHardening` on their own repo was a legitimate zero-match rather than a cycle-induced false clean. It was not reproduced here (the scan returns candidates on this repo), and this run's return shape (`{candidates}`) differs from the array the reporter saw on 6.132.0. Confirm by running the scan against a fixture containing an `api/` route with a known finding, both before and after the require-order fix.
- Do not fix item 3 by suppressing Node warnings. The undefined bindings are real for whichever generator loads mid-cycle.
- Item 1 belongs to #3044. Do not fold a sample-file writer into this record.

## Original request

Four friction points in a /flow build-review-wrap-up run under worktree isolation (claude-tweaks 6.132.0)

Component: claude-tweaks plugin (skills/build/dispatch.md, bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js, bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js, bin/log-decision.js)
Kind: defect

## Summary

A single-record `/claude-tweaks:flow` run (worktree-isolated session, Windows, plugin 6.132.0) hit four plugin-side issues. Item 3 is the most important: it looks like a silent false-clean in review's Step 6.6 security-hardening pass.

## 1. `build/dispatch.md`'s AC-forwarding sample path is unwritable from a worktree session

`skills/build/dispatch.md` ("Standing AC-forwarding verification") tells the run to copy the first reviewer prompt to `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/sdd-dispatch-sample.txt`. In a worktree-isolated session the harness's Write tool refuses that path ("Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path"), because the run dir is anchored in the main checkout. Workaround used: write inside the worktree, then `cp`. Suggest: document a sanctioned writer (as for `log-decision.js`/`stage-item.js`), or name a worktree-local sample path.

## 2. `computeDiffFacts` input shape vs. its documented call

`skills/build/dispatch.md` ("Whole-branch review model") says to compute diff facts "via `bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js`'s `computeDiffFacts` over the branch's `git diff --numstat` output". The function expects the parsed `{path, additions, deletions}[]` array (`blast-radius-cli.js`'s `parseNumstat` shape). Passing the raw numstat string throws `TypeError: (files || []).map is not a function` at `bin/lib/issues/blast-radius.js:91`. Suggest: export or document the parser in the same sentence, or have `resolve-profile.js` accept `--numstat`.

## 3. `scanSecurityHardening` appears to fail silently on a circular import

Running review Step 6.6's documented invocation:

```
node -e "const {scanSecurityHardening}=require('<plugin>/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js'); console.log(JSON.stringify(scanSecurityHardening(process.cwd())))"
```

printed `[]`, preceded by repeated warnings: `Accessing non-existent property 'listTrackedSourceFiles' of module exports inside circular dependency` (also `isGlobDiscoveredTestFile`, `extractModuleExports`, `escapeRegExp`, `listTrackedFiles`). It returned 0 candidates repo-wide on a repo with an `api/` routes tree. If those helpers resolve to `undefined` because of the cycle, every per-review security-hardening pass reports a false clean. Suggest: break the cycle (lazy require), and have the pass fail loudly when its helpers are unresolved.

## 4. `log-decision.js --reversibility` rejects the documented parenthesised form

`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s mandatory log lines read e.g. `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).` Passing that as `--reversibility "high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)"` fails: `--reversibility must be one of high|med|low|n/a`. Suggest: accept a trailing parenthetical, or document that the qualifier goes into `--text`.

## Environment

claude-tweaks 6.132.0; Claude Code on Windows 11, Git Bash; worktree-isolated session (`worktree-always` policy).

**Plugin version:** 6.132.0

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

**Related:** #3027, #3071

## Current State

plugin/bin/lib/visual-decide/cli.js's pidAlive() signals the target PID with kill(pid, 0) to decide liveness. The test kills the server's PID with SIGKILL, waits 300ms, then calls stop. In this sandbox (PID 1 is a Firecracker process_api init, not a standard reaper), the killed child becomes a zombie whose PID still answers kill(pid,0) successfully for longer than 300ms, so pidAlive reports "alive" even though the process is dead. cmdStop then takes the live-process branch: sends SIGTERM (a no-op on a zombie), waits up to 3000ms via waitFor for the server-stopped marker or !pidAlive, times out, and still exits 0 printing "stopped" — but the server-stopped marker file (written only by the server's own SIGTERM handler) never gets created, since the zombie can't run code. Net effect: stop exits 0 with "stopped" but no marker file, violating the stale-PID-tolerance contract the test name describes.

## Deliverables

Either (a) treat a waitFor timeout in cmdStop as cause to also write the server-stopped marker defensively (matching the dead-pid branch's own behavior at cli.js:190-197), or (b) make pidAlive zombie-aware (e.g. checking /proc/{pid}/stat state Z on Linux) so it correctly reports a zombie as not-meaningfully-alive for this CLI's purposes. Re-run the test 3x in this same sandbox type to confirm no regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- node --test tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js passes reliably (3/3 consecutive runs) in a container without a reaping init (PID 1 not a standard init/tini).
- No change to the already-passing EPERM/ESRCH pidAlive semantics documented at cli.js:48-52.
- Existing stop/status test coverage for the non-zombie dead-PID path (ESRCH) still passes unchanged.

## Release Note

No user-visible change — internal test/CLI reliability fix for the visual-decide stop command in containers without a reaping init.

## Current State

`verify.js` only writes the pass stamp on a clean exit 0 across the full resolved check set. This
checkout is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → true, ~53 commits), so 3
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <pinned-sha> HEAD` precondition tests fail deterministically
regardless of diff content, plus one unrelated stale-PID process-liveness test
(`tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js`) that also reproduces on isolated re-run in this
sandbox. Every review of a docs-only or low-risk record in this environment re-derives the same
"these 4 failures are pre-existing and unrelated" conclusion by hand (isolation runs, direct
`git merge-base` reproduction) because the runner's stamp is binary and never reflects a
declared-pre-existing-failure allowance — this cost was paid identically by at least one prior
attempt on #1350's own history and again by this run.

## Deliverables

Extend `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`'s declaration format with a `preExisting` (or similarly
named) list of known-failing test files/patterns — analogous to the existing `flaky.files`
mechanism — that `verify.js` treats as non-blocking for stamp purposes: when every failing test in
a run is in this declared set, write the pass stamp (with a field noting which pre-existing
failures were present) instead of leaving the run permanently un-stamped.

## Acceptance Criteria

A run whose only failures are listed in the new declaration still writes `claude-tweaks-verify-pass.json`
(scoped, as today), with a field recording the declared pre-existing failures that were present; a
run with any other failure still does not stamp.

declared pre-existing test failures (e.g. a shallow clone).

groups.body:
**Skill:** node-test-output-evidence | **Section:** Key Patterns | **Category:** drift | **Classification:** restructural | **Confidence:** high

Verified-as-of: f062f6938b2f1b50de9ed00c78dae26a061c196a

## Current State

Also affects: `Decision Framework`

plugin/bin/lib/verify/baseline.js lines 223-230 explicitly tolerate cancelled > 0 in the full run's accounting (`entries !== counts.fail + cancelled`), and the code comment there states "A cancelled HEAD test is then held to the usual evidence: it fails at base, or shows its own pass in isolation" — contradicting the skill's claim that a full run with a cancelled test is never adjudicated and a pass is never reached. The zero-cancelled rule the skill describes belongs to accountedFamily (used only for each isolated single-file rerun, lines 157-164 and its call sites at ~280/326/343), not the full-run extraction this subsection and Decision Framework row describe.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
An extracted list of failures cannot report that it missed one. `adjudicate` refuses to classify unless:

- the spec `test at` entries (`specEntryCount`) add up to the summary's `ℹ fail N`;
- every failing entry or TAP `not ok` block names a test file (`countUnmatchedFailures` returns 0);
- the summary counts parse at all, because a truncated log has none;
- `ℹ cancelled` (spec) or `# cancelled` (TAP) reads 0 in a single-file log.

The listing and `ℹ fail` do not count the same things. A cancelled test, for example one that timed out, is listed but not counted, so a full run containing one is never adjudicated. That outcome is fail-closed, and a pass is never reached. A diagnostic that says the test timed out or was cancelled (`INCONCLUSIVE_RE`) means the test did not finish, which proves nothing about whether it fails.
```

**Proposed:**
```
An extracted list of failures cannot report that it missed one. `adjudicate` refuses to classify the full run unless:

- the spec `test at` entries (`specEntryCount`) add up to the summary's `ℹ fail N` plus its `ℹ cancelled` count;
- every failing entry or TAP `not ok` block names a test file (`countUnmatchedFailures` returns 0);
- the summary counts parse at all, because a truncated log has none.

The listing and `ℹ fail` do not count the same things — a cancelled test, for example one that timed out, is listed but not counted, so the full run's entries must reconcile against `ℹ fail` plus `ℹ cancelled`, not `ℹ fail` alone. A cancelled test does not by itself block adjudication of the full run: it is held to the usual per-file evidence (it fails at base, or shows its own pass in isolation). Only that isolated single-file rerun must itself show `ℹ cancelled`/`# cancelled` at 0 (`accountedFamily`) to count as evidence — a rerun that times out or cancels proves nothing and that file stays unclassified. A diagnostic that says the test timed out or was cancelled (`INCONCLUSIVE_RE`) means the test did not finish, which proves nothing about whether it fails.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The "Reconcile the failing list against an independent count" subsection and the Decision Framework's cancelled-count row both state that a non-zero cancelled count blocks adjudication of the full run and that "a pass is never reached" — plugin/bin/lib/verify/baseline.js's adjudicate() (lines 223-230) actually tolerates a non-zero ℹ cancelled count in the full run, requiring only that entries equal fail + cancelled, then routes the cancelled test's file through the same per-file isolated-rerun evidence as any other failure (ranCleanly/baselineInIsolation, lines ~319-356), which CAN return verdict: 'pass'. The zero-cancelled requirement (accountedFamily, cancelledCount(text, family) !== 0) applies only to each isolated single-file rerun log, not to the full run's own extraction/eligibility check. Fix both the Key Patterns subsection (oldString/newString above) and the Decision Framework row ("A non-zero cancelled count, a timeout diagnostic, or a runner-level `ℹ Error:` | Did not finish, or failed outside any test. No evidence") to the same corrected distinction: a non-zero cancelled count in the full run does not by itself mean no evidence; it only does for an isolated single-file rerun.

Origin: /claude-tweaks:flow #3101-#3104 run 2026-10-10T190327-spec-3101-3102-3103-3104. PR #3107's CI caught what local verification missed.

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`tests/release-lifecycle-byte-budget.test.js` measures `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` and `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` with `Buffer.byteLength(fs.readFileSync(...))`. That counts raw bytes, so on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf` the CRLF line endings inflate both counts past their caps. The test therefore always fails at base there.

`verify.js`'s baseline adjudication then counts that file as pre-existing. A real regression is invisible locally on Windows. In run 2026-10-10T190327, #3101 grew `scan-procedures.md` to 43840 B against its 42466 B cap. Local verification passed four times, and only Linux CI on PR #3107 caught it (fixed in 58625fcde).

## Deliverables

- Normalize `\r\n` to `\n` before measuring in `release-lifecycle-byte-budget.test.js`, so the count matches the LF blob CI sees.
- Sweep `tests/` for other raw-byte budget checks over skill or doc files, such as `Buffer.byteLength(fs.readFileSync(...))` or `fs.statSync(...).size` compared against a constant, and give them the same normalization. Follow the `windows-checkout-test-parity` project skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a Windows CRLF checkout, `release-lifecycle-byte-budget.test.js` passes at a base whose LF blobs are under budget, and fails when a file's LF size is over budget.
- [ ] No byte-budget test under `tests/` compares a raw CRLF byte count against an LF-derived ceiling.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

Origin: v6.138.0 release review (lens 3d performance), refs #3043
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Before any rerun starts, `adjudicate` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/baseline.js:256-257`) calls `git.fileExistsAt` (`git cat-file -e`) and `git.sameAtBase` per failing file. `sameAtBase` (lines 52-57) adds `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse sha:file` and `hash-object`, and the toplevel lookup repeats a root `adjudicate` already holds from `git.repoRoot()`. That is up to four serial `execFileSync` spawns per file. On this Windows box's ~98-file baseline, the spawn cost alone is seconds of dead time. This is unmeasured.

Evidence: v6.138.0 release whole-branch review, staged `review-8.md`. Reproduced by both 3d agents.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Existence and sameness for all failing files resolved in a constant number of git calls (e.g. one `cat-file --batch-check` plus one `hash-object --stdin-paths`), with the repo root passed in rather than re-resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An adjudication over N failing files makes a number of pre-run git spawns that does not grow with N (asserted through the injected git seam).
- [ ] Verdicts on the existing baseline test fixtures are unchanged.

_Filed by `review` via specShapedBody._

## Release Note

Verification baseline checks now run faster on large failure sets by batching their per-file git probes.

Origin: ledger resolve gate
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`verify.js --baseline` (#3043) classifies a failing test file as `baseline-flaky` when it fails in the full run but passes when re-run alone at HEAD, and prints one `CAVEAT: baseline-flaky:` line. The verdict goes nowhere else:
- It is never counted into the count stamp's `flakyHits`. That is the counter #1925's allowlisted retry feeds, and it drives the five-hit `flaky-allowlist` escalation caveat.
- It never stages a proposal to add the file to `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`'s `flaky.files`.

A file that keeps passing only in isolation is therefore invisible beyond each run's own CAVEAT.

Evidence: #3043's final whole-branch review follow-up I3 (ledger row 17). In the live runs, `tests/bin-lib/gif/palette.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/file-lock.test.js` each landed as baseline-flaky.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Count every `baselineAdjudicated.flakyPassed` file into `flakyHits` exactly as a retried allowlisted file is counted, in the count stamp's existing shape.
- [ ] A file whose hits reach the escalation threshold without being on `flaky.files` stages a `flaky-allowlist` proposal for the Review Console. It is never applied silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After two adjudicated runs in which the same file is baseline-flaky, the count stamp's `flakyHits` holds that file at 2.
- [ ] At the threshold, a staged allowlist proposal names the file and its hit count, and `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` is unchanged until the proposal is approved.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._

## Release Note

Flaky results from baseline verification now count toward the flaky-allowlist escalation threshold.

Surface: infra

## Current State

The audit the original request asks for has a known answer at shaping time: a repo-wide `git grep -i -E 'thinking_?disabled|between_tools'` returns zero hits. Nothing in `plugin/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `evals/`, or the project's `.claude/` references either spelling.

claude-tweaks does not set a thinking mode anywhere. It controls models through two settings:

- Agent and routine frontmatter set `model:` and `effort:` only. `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` uses `model: sonnet` and `effort: medium`. Every `plugin/skills/*/routine-template.yml` carries a `model:` line, for example `plugin/skills/specify/routine-template.yml:7` `model: claude-sonnet-5`.
- Subagent dispatches resolve a model profile through `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js`. The profiles (`plugin/bin/lib/model-profiles/profiles.js:15-18`) carry `model` and `effort` fields only, and effort reaches the agent as a prompt line, not an API thinking setting (`profiles.js:27-29`).

The external change: Claude Sonnet 5.5 renames the no-upfront-thinking setting from `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools` (source in the original request below).

`docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is where this repo records per-model deltas that affect how skills are authored. It currently has a Fable 5.1 entry (line 233) and no Sonnet 5.5 entry.

## Deliverables

1. Re-run the zero-usage audit at build time (the grep above, repo-wide, both spellings) and record the result in this record's closing comment.
2. Add one short Sonnet 5.5 bullet to the "Model-version prompting notes" section of `docs/skill-authoring.md`. It should state the `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools` rename, cite the migration guide, and say that claude-tweaks sets no thinking mode today (model and effort only), so nothing needs migrating. Any future agent, routine template, or profile that adds a thinking setting should use `between_tools` when targeting Sonnet 5.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The build-time grep for `thinkingdisabled` (case-insensitive, with and without an underscore) returns zero hits outside the new note.
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Model-version prompting notes section carries a Sonnet 5.5 bullet naming both spellings and linking the migration guide.
- CLAUDE.md is unchanged. The note belongs in the model-version section, not the always-loaded file, which has a line budget.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This records the Sonnet 5.5 thinking-setting rename in claude-tweaks' authoring notes; no configuration needed migrating.

## Technical Approach

A documentation-only change. Re-run the grep, then add the bullet next to the existing Fable 5.1 entry, following its source-cited format. If the build-time grep unexpectedly finds a usage, migrate it in the same change, scoped to settings that target `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and list it in the closing comment.

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — Model-version prompting notes section gains the Sonnet 5.5 bullet
- `plugin/bin/lib/model-profiles/profiles.js` — profile fields (model, effort) confirmed to carry no thinking setting
- `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` — the one shipped agent's model and effort frontmatter

## Gotchas

- The original request assumed claude-tweaks "may still reference the old flag". The shaping-time grep contradicts that, so no migration is expected. Do not invent a thinking setting just to have something to rename.
- Routine templates pin `claude-sonnet-5`, not `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Bumping their model is a separate decision, out of scope here.

## Original request

Audit claude-tweaks configs for the thinkingdisabled rename

Current State:
- Claude Sonnet 5.5 renames the no-upfront-thinking setting from `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools`.
- claude-tweaks defines multiple subagents/skills with model and thinking settings that may still reference the old flag.

Deliverables:
- Audit claude-tweaks' agent/skill definitions for any `thinkingdisabled` usage.
- Migrate any found usages to `between_tools` when targeting claude-sonnet-5-5.

Acceptance Criteria:
- No remaining `thinkingdisabled` references that target Sonnet 5.5.
- A short note in CLAUDE.md or the relevant skill doc about the rename.

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide
